cards.remember: Nonconforming means legal at the start. Never-legal is just a violation.

question.q: The store at 1402 Loblolly Boulevard opened legally before a 2010 rezoning to single-family. What is its status?
options: A nonconforming use that may continue
An illegal use that must close
A special exception needing board approval
A variance that ends when the store is sold
question.why: A use that was legal when it began and no longer complies is grandfathered as nonconforming. A use that never complied is a violation.

items.title: Variance, special exception, rezoning, spot zoning

cards.idea: A variance relaxes a dimensional rule for hardship unique to the land. A special exception allows a use the ordinance already lists, if conditions are met. Rezoning changes the district. Spot zoning favors one parcel against the plan; generally invalid.
cards.scene: An oddly shaped lot on Slash Pine Road can't fit a house at the 25-foot rear setback, a scenario figure. The owner seeks a variance to build at 18 feet. The use, a house, stays allowed.
cards.trap: The exam swaps variance and special exception. A variance relaxes a rule: how. A special exception permits a use the ordinance anticipates: what. A homeowner wanting a day care in a residential district needs a special exception.
cards.remember: Variance changes how you build. Special exception permits what you do.

question.q: A homeowner wants to run a day care in a residential district whose ordinance allows it if conditions are met and the board approves. What does she need?
options: A variance
Spot zoning
A rezoning
A special exception
question.why: A special exception permits a use the ordinance already anticipates, once conditions are met. A variance relaxes a dimensional rule like a setback.

cards.idea: Subdivision rules control how land becomes lots: streets, drainage, easements, lot sizes. The developer records a plat. Building permits come before construction, major alteration or demolition. After final inspection comes a certificate of occupancy; without it, no legal occupancy.
cards.scene: A house on Spoonbill Point Drive has a garage converted to a bedroom, with no permit on record. The room may need removal or after-the-fact permitting at the buyer's cost. A listing licensee who knows and stays quiet has a disclosure problem.
cards.trap: The exam calls unpermitted work the buyer's risk alone. In Florida residential sales, a seller and licensee who know of a fact that materially affects value and isn't readily observable must disclose it.
cards.remember: Known unpermitted work that affects value must be disclosed.

question.q: A listing licensee knows a Spoonbill Point Drive garage conversion was never permitted. What must she do?
options: Nothing, since checking permits is the buyer's job
Disclose it, since it materially affects value
Disclose it only if the buyer asks
Refuse the listing until the room is removed
question.why: Florida requires sellers and licensees to disclose known facts that materially affect value and aren't readily observable. Unpermitted work isn't the buyer's risk alone.

cards.idea: Florida adopted one statewide building code in 2002, after Hurricane Andrew in 1992 exposed weak construction. The Florida Building Commission maintains it. Local governments enforce it and may amend it only in limited ways.
cards.scene: A builder in Broward County works in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, which also covers Miami-Dade. Windows and doors there need product approvals other areas don't, under the same statewide code.
cards.trap: The exam says each Florida county writes its own building code. Florida has one statewide code; counties enforce it.
cards.remember: One statewide code, written by the state, enforced locally.

question.q: Who writes the building code a Florida county enforces?
options: Each county commission
The local building official
The state, through the Florida Building Code
FEMA
question.why: Florida has one statewide code, maintained by the Florida Building Commission. Counties enforce it and may amend it only in limited ways.

cards.idea: Deed restrictions are private limits in deeds or a subdivision's recorded declaration, enforced by an HOA or neighbors through lawsuits. Zoning is public, enforced by government. When they conflict, the more restrictive one governs.
cards.scene: Zoning lets an owner build a two-story house. The subdivision's deed restrictions allow only one story. The owner builds one story, because the stricter rule controls.
cards.trap: The exam says zoning overrides private restrictions. It doesn't. The stricter rule controls, whichever source it comes from.
cards.remember: When zoning and deed restrictions conflict, the stricter one wins.

question.q: Zoning allows two-story homes, but the deed restrictions allow only one story. What may the owner build?
options: One story, because the stricter rule controls
Two stories, because zoning overrides private rules
Two stories, if the city issues a permit
Whatever the HOA votes to allow that year
question.why: When private restrictions and zoning conflict, the more restrictive governs. Zoning doesn't override deed restrictions.

cards.idea: FEMA's NFIP maps flood risk and offers flood insurance; standard homeowner's policies don't cover flood. A and V zones are Special Flood Hazard Areas, with a 1 percent annual chance of flooding. Federally backed loans there require flood insurance.
cards.scene: A buyer closes in three weeks on 88 Spoonbill Point Drive, in Zone AE, with an FHA loan. Flood insurance is mandatory. Because the policy is bought with the loan, the usual 30-day wait doesn't delay closing.
cards.trap: The exam says Zone X means no flood risk. It means lower mapped risk, and a large share of flood claims come from outside the SFHA. Insurance isn't mandatory there but can still be wise.
cards.remember: Zone X is lower risk, not no risk.

question.q: A home sits in Zone X. Which statement is accurate?
options: The home has no flood risk
Flood insurance is mandatory for any loan
Flood insurance isn't mandatory, but flood risk still exists
A standard homeowner's policy covers flood there
question.why: Zone X means moderate to minimal mapped risk, not none, and many flood claims come from outside the SFHA. Standard homeowner's policies don't cover flood anywhere.

cards.idea: Along Florida's sandy beaches, the state has drawn a coastal construction control line. Seaward of it, construction, major repairs and seawalls need a Florida DEP permit on top of local permits, with tougher storm and dune standards.
cards.scene: A buyer wants to tear down and rebuild an older beach cottage at 9 Spoonbill Point Drive, seaward of the CCCL. The county permit isn't enough. The DEP permit may demand a new footprint, a higher floor and pilings, and take months.
cards.trap: The exam calls the CCCL a federal line. It's a Florida line, set and permitted by Florida DEP.
cards.remember: The CCCL is Florida's line, permitted by Florida DEP.

question.q: Who issues the extra permit needed to rebuild seaward of the coastal construction control line?
options: FEMA
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
Only the county building department
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection
question.why: The CCCL is a Florida line, and building seaward of it needs a Florida DEP permit on top of local permits.

cards.idea: Radon is a natural radioactive gas from uranium breaking down in soil and rock. It enters through foundation cracks, unseen and unsmelled. Florida requires a specific radon notice at or before the contract to sell or rent any building.
cards.scene: A landlord leases out a commercial warehouse. The lease still needs Florida's radon notice. Neither the landlord nor a home seller has to test; the law requires the notice, not a test.
cards.trap: The exam says radon disclosure applies only to homes. It applies to the sale or rental of any building, residential or commercial.
cards.remember: Radon notice: any building, sale or rental. A notice, not a test.

question.q: Which transaction requires Florida's radon notice?
options: Only sales of single-family homes
The sale or rental of any building, residential or commercial
Only buildings with foundation cracks
Only buildings that failed a radon test
question.why: The notice applies to the sale or rental of any building. The law requires the notice, not a test.

cards.idea: Lead-based paint was banned for residential use in 1978. For housing built before 1978, sellers and landlords disclose known lead, give the EPA pamphlet and sign a Lead Warning Statement. Buyers get a 10-day inspection opportunity. Licensees share the duty.
cards.scene: A 1962 house on Loblolly Boulevard is listed. The seller never tested and knows of no lead. She still gives the pamphlet, the warning statement and a disclosure saying no known lead. The buyer still gets 10 days to inspect.
cards.trap: The seller says, "I've never tested, so there's nothing to disclose." The pre-1978 construction date triggers the rule, not her knowledge. What she knows sets the disclosure's content, not whether it's given.
cards.remember: Built before 1978 means disclose. Knowledge sets the content, not the duty.

question.q: The seller of a 1962 house on Loblolly Boulevard never tested for lead and knows of none. What is required?
options: The pamphlet, warning statement and disclosure stating no known lead
Nothing, since no lead is known
A lead test before the house can be listed
Disclosure only if the buyer has young children
question.why: The 1978 construction date triggers the rule, not the seller's knowledge. "No known lead" is a disclosure, not an exemption.

cards.idea: Asbestos is dangerous mainly when disturbed, so renovation is the risky moment; sealing it in place is often safer. Known material mold falls under the general disclosure duty. Under CERCLA, owners can owe cleanup costs they didn't cause.
cards.scene: An investor wants to buy a former dry cleaner at 2300 Loblolly Boulevard. Dry-cleaning solvents commonly contaminate groundwater. Without a Phase I environmental site assessment before closing, she could owe a cleanup costing more than the building.
cards.trap: The exam says the polluter pays, so the new owner is safe. Under CERCLA the current owner can be liable regardless of who caused it. A Phase I before purchase supports the innocent landowner defense.
cards.remember: Under CERCLA the current owner can pay. Do a Phase I first.

question.q: Before buying the former dry cleaner at 2300 Loblolly Boulevard, how can an investor protect against cleanup liability?
options: Rely on the rule that only the polluter pays
Conduct a Phase I environmental site assessment
Order a radon test
Take title through an LLC
question.why: CERCLA can make the current owner liable regardless of who caused the contamination. A Phase I before purchase supports the innocent landowner defense.

cards.idea: Much of Florida sits on limestone, which can dissolve and collapse into sinkholes. Insurers must cover catastrophic ground cover collapse; broader sinkhole coverage is generally optional. Filling wetlands generally needs Army Corps and state permits.
cards.scene: A buyer finds a cheap two-acre lot on Slash Pine Road. A survey shows 1.5 acres are jurisdictional wetlands. The buildable area may be a quarter of what she expected, and the price reflects that.
cards.trap: The exam says standard homeowner's insurance covers all Florida sinkhole damage. Required coverage is only for catastrophic ground cover collapse, a sudden collapse making the home uninhabitable. Lesser damage needs optional coverage.
cards.remember: Required sinkhole coverage is catastrophic ground cover collapse only.

question.q: A Florida home has sinkhole damage but stays habitable. When is the damage covered?
options: Always, since all sinkhole damage must be covered
Only if the home has a homestead exemption
Never, since sinkholes can't be insured in Florida
When the owner bought optional sinkhole coverage
question.why: Florida requires coverage only for catastrophic ground cover collapse, which makes the home uninhabitable. Lesser damage generally needs optional coverage.

questions.q: In the sale of a house on Cocoplum Way, which person needs a Florida real estate license?
options: The appraiser valuing it for the lender
The loan originator arranging the mortgage
The sales associate who listed it
The title agent searching the record
questions.why: Listing property for another is brokerage, which the real estate license covers. The others are regulated, but not by the real estate license or FREC.

questions.q: A sales associate who sells homes on Buttonwood Street is asked to list a strip center. What does Florida require?
options: A separate commercial real estate license
Nothing more; her license already covers it
A broker's license, since commercial is broker-only
Her own brokerage office for commercial work
questions.why: Florida has no separate commercial license, so the same sales associate license covers both. Competence and her broker's supervision are what limit her.

questions.q: The listing agent on Marlberry Lane prepares a CMA for the seller. Which is true under Florida law?
options: She may prepare it and be paid, but not call it an appraisal
She may not give any opinion of value
She may call it an appraisal if it is thorough enough
She needs the Appraisal Board's approval first
questions.why: Florida lets a licensee prepare a CMA and even be paid for it, as long as it is never called an appraisal. Appraisers are licensed separately, under their own board.

questions.q: A duplex owner on Buttonwood Street pays a friend a share of the first month's rent for finding tenants. What is the friend doing?
options: Helping informally, so no license is needed
Acting as a community association manager
Nothing regulated, because no sale occurred
Brokerage activity that requires a license
questions.why: Under Florida law, renting or leasing for another for compensation is brokerage. Without a license, the friend is acting illegally.

questions.q: Which body regulates loan originators in Florida?
options: The Florida Real Estate Commission
The Office of Financial Regulation
The Division of Real Estate within DBPR
The Florida Real Estate Appraisal Board
questions.why: Mortgage brokering and loan origination fall under Chapter 494 of the Florida Statutes, regulated by the Office of Financial Regulation. FREC and DBPR do not license them.

questions.q: A company records a plat dividing a tract west of Marlberry Lane into lots and sells them empty to builders. What is it?
options: A developer
A speculative builder
A subdivider
A custom builder
questions.why: Dividing land into lots with a recorded plat is subdividing. It would be a developer only if it added improvements like roads, utilities or houses.

questions.q: An owner hires a real estate counselor to advise whether to hold or sell. When is the counselor's fee earned?
options: Only if the owner decides to sell
Only once a buyer is under contract
Only if the advice raises the property's value
For the advice, whether or not a sale happens
questions.why: A counselor is paid for the advice itself. A fee that depends on a sale is a brokerage fee and requires a brokerage license.

questions.q: A distribution warehouse used for storage sits at the edge of town. Which category is it?
options: Industrial
Commercial
Special-purpose
Agricultural
questions.why: Warehousing and distribution are industrial uses. A business using the building doesn't make it commercial; selling to the public would.

ch1-the-florida-regulators-at-a-first-lo.title: The Florida regulators, at a first look

questions.q: A buyer complains that a sales associate misled her. Who decides the penalty?
options: The Division of Real Estate's investigators
The Office of Financial Regulation
The Florida Real Estate Commission
The local REALTOR® association
questions.why: Investigating a complaint is the department's job, but deciding the penalty is the commission's. FREC is the rule-making and judging body.

questions.q: A Florida licensee breaks the REALTOR® Code of Ethics but no Florida law or FREC rule. What can FREC do about the Code breach?
options: Suspend the license for the Code breach
Nothing; FREC enforces Florida law, not the Code
Order DBPR to revoke the license
Fine the licensee under its own rules
questions.why: NAR's Code of Ethics is a private standard; breaking it can cost association membership. FREC enforces Chapter 475 and its own rules.

questions.q: A CPM holder with no Florida real estate license offers to lease units on Buttonwood Street for a percentage of the rent. Which is true?
options: The CPM lets her lease units for others
She may lease if she also holds the GRI
She may lease units but not collect rent
She needs a license unless an exemption applies
questions.why: A designation adds no legal authority. Leasing for others for compensation still requires a Florida real estate license unless an exemption applies.

questions.q: What is the stated purpose of Florida's real estate license law?
options: To protect the public
To limit the number of agents
To protect licensees from unqualified competitors
To maintain high commission rates
questions.why: Florida licenses practitioners to protect the public, under its police power. The other choices describe protecting the profession, which is not the purpose.

ch2-what-counts-as-real-estate-services.title: What counts as real estate services

questions.q: For a promised fee, an unlicensed person shows a house on Pond Apple Road to three prospects. No offer is made. Did he perform real estate services?
options: No, because no deal closed
No, because he was never actually paid
Yes, because attempting a sale for a fee counts
Only if the seller signed a listing agreement
questions.why: Florida's definition covers offering and attempting, for compensation paid, promised or expected. A deal doesn't have to close.

questions.q: A neighbor on Wax Myrtle Lane finds a buyer for a friend's house and receives the friend's boat. It is his only deal ever. Did he need a license?
options: No, because a boat isn't compensation
No, because it was a single transaction
Only if the boat's value passed a set amount
Yes, because a boat is valuable consideration
questions.why: Valuable consideration includes anything of value, and Florida has no one-time exception. He acted for another and procured a buyer.

questions.q: A son holds power of attorney for his mother's house on Beautyberry Court. Which act is exempt?
options: Signing the deed on his mother's behalf
Finding a buyer for a neighbor's condo for a fee
Taking a finder's fee for introducing a buyer
Marketing friends' homes for a share of the price
questions.why: A power of attorney lets him sign contracts and conveyances for his mother. It doesn't let him find buyers for others for a fee.

questions.q: Which best describes a broker associate?
options: A sales associate with extra experience
A person with a broker's license working under another broker
A temporary license held before the broker exam
A broker who employs sales associates
questions.why: A broker associate holds a full broker's license but chooses to work under another broker, the way a sales associate does.

ch2-qualifying-for-a-sales-associate-lic.title: Qualifying for a sales associate license

questions.q: A student on Pond Apple Road passes the end-of-course exam for the 63-hour course. What is her status?
options: Licensed, pending her broker's signature
Licensed as an inactive sales associate
Eligible to practice under a broker's supervision
Eligible for the state exam, not yet licensed
questions.why: Passing the course exam makes her eligible but doesn't license her. The state exam is a separate test.

questions.q: An applicant pled no contest to a misdemeanor and adjudication was withheld. What must he do on the application?
options: Leave it off, since he wasn't convicted
Withdraw, since any record disqualifies him
Disclose it truthfully
Disclose it only if it was a felony
questions.why: On the Florida application, no contest pleas and withheld adjudication must be disclosed. Concealment is itself evidence the applicant isn't honest and trustworthy.

questions.q: A new licensee passed the state exam yesterday but has no employing broker. May she show a listing on Beautyberry Court today?
options: No, she needs an active license under an employing broker
Yes, the license is active once issued
Yes, if the seller agrees in writing
No, she must first finish post-licensing education
questions.why: A sales associate's license is active only when tied to an employing broker. Without one, she holds a license but cannot practice.

questions.q: A sales associate misses the post-licensing course before her first renewal. What happens to her license?
options: It becomes involuntarily inactive
It is suspended until she finishes
It becomes null and void
It renews if she pays a late fee
questions.why: Missing post-licensing before the first renewal makes the license null and void. It ceases to exist rather than going inactive.

questions.q: What does a sales associate owe at her first renewal?
options: 14 hours of CE plus post-licensing
14 hours of CE only
Core Law only
Post-licensing only, no regular CE
questions.why: Post-licensing replaces continuing education at the first renewal. The 14 hours of CE start with the renewal after that.

questions.q: A broker licensed in a mutual recognition state, and living there, wants a Florida license. What must she do?
options: Nothing; her license is valid in Florida
Pass an exam on Florida real estate law
Take the pre-license course and full exam
Move to Florida first
questions.why: Mutual recognition lets her skip the pre-license course and full state exam, but she still passes an exam on Florida law and meets the other requirements.

questions.q: An unlicensed person shows homes on weekends for a share of a licensee's commissions. What offense is he committing?
options: A second-degree misdemeanor
A first-degree misdemeanor
A third-degree felony
No offense, since the licensee pays him
questions.why: Performing real estate services for compensation without a license is a third-degree felony in Florida. Most license-law violations are misdemeanors; this one is the exception.

ch3-two-bodies-one-job-dbpr-and-frec.title: Two bodies, one job: DBPR and FREC

questions.q: Which describes FREC's seven members?
options: Five brokers and two consumer members
Four brokers, one broker or sales associate, two consumer members
Seven licensed brokers
Four brokers and three consumer members
questions.why: FREC has four brokers, one broker or sales associate, and two consumer members who have never been brokers or sales associates.

ch3-where-the-rules-live-chapter-475-and.title: Where the rules live: Chapter 475 and Rule 61J2

questions.q: A licensee breaks a FREC rule in Chapter 61J2 on conduct the statute never mentions. What is the result?
options: No violation, since only statutes bind
A violation only if the Legislature approves the rule
A violation of the license law
A warning, since rules are advisory
questions.why: Breaking a Commission rule is itself a violation of the license law. Within its scope, a FREC rule binds exactly as the statute does.

ch3-what-a-license-can-be-active-inactiv.title: What a license can be: active, inactive, null and void

questions.q: A licensee on Simpson Stopper Way forgets to renew and does nothing to reactivate for more than 2 years. What is his license's status?
options: Null and void
Involuntarily inactive
Voluntarily inactive
Active but delinquent
questions.why: A missed renewal makes the license involuntarily inactive. Left unreactivated past 2 years, it becomes null and void.

ch3-renewal-and-education-across-the-lic.title: Renewal and education across the license cycle

questions.q: A broker associate past her first renewal hasn't finished her 14 CE hours by her September 30 expiration. What is her status on October 1?
options: Null and void
Suspended pending a hearing
Voluntarily inactive
Involuntarily inactive
questions.why: Missing CE at a later renewal makes the license involuntarily inactive, which can be reactivated. Only missing post-licensing at the first renewal voids it.

questions.q: A licensee moves and doesn't update her address. A complaint is sent to the old address. Which is true?
options: The notice is invalid until she receives it
She is bound, because notice to the address on file counts
DBPR must re-serve her at her new address
She has 10 days after learning of it to object
questions.why: Florida law treats DBPR notices sent to the last address on file as properly served. Not receiving it because it went to an old address is no defense.

ch3-registering-a-brokerage-that-is-a-co.title: Registering a brokerage that is a company

questions.q: In a brokerage organized as a limited partnership, who must be an active broker?
options: Every limited partner
Only the largest investor
At least one general partner
Every partner, general or limited
questions.why: A limited partnership needs at least one general partner who is an active broker. Limited partners, who invest but don't manage, need no license.

questions.q: A sales associate wants her own trade name, and her broker approves. May she register one?
options: Yes, with written broker approval
Yes, if it is filed with the Department of State
Yes, if it includes the broker's name
No, a sales associate cannot have a trade name
questions.why: A sales associate cannot operate a brokerage, so she cannot have a trade name for one. The license and the business belong to the broker.

questions.q: A sales associate's two unrelated brokers both consent to her working for each of them. Which is true?
options: She may, since both brokers consented
She may, if she obtains a group license
She may not; consent doesn't create a second employer
She may, if she holds multiple licenses
questions.why: An associate works for one employer at a time. The only exception, a group license, covers related owner-developer entities, not unrelated brokers.

ch4-agency-basics-principal-customer-and.title: Agency basics: principal, customer and fiduciary

questions.q: For weeks a buyer discusses homes on Firewheel Road with a licensee and calls her "my agent." Nothing was ever signed. What relationship most likely exists?
options: Single agency, implied from their conduct
Transaction broker
No relationship, so she owes him nothing
Dual agency, since she also talks to sellers
questions.why: Florida requires single agency to be established in writing, so conduct alone doesn't create it and the licensee is presumed a transaction broker. Implied agency is the generic-textbook answer that Florida narrows.

questions.q: A licensee is single agent for the seller of a house on Saw Palmetto Trail. A buyer tours the house with her. What is the buyer's status?
options: A customer, dealt with honestly but not represented
A co-principal sharing the seller's protections
A principal, because she showed him the house
Outside the transaction, so owed no duties
questions.why: The seller is the principal and anyone else in the transaction is a customer, owed honest dealing but not fiduciary duties. Showing a buyer a house doesn't turn him into a principal.

questions.q: A single-agent listing on Spanish Stopper Drive expires unsold. During the listing, the seller told the licensee why he was moving. What happens to that confidentiality?
options: It survives the end of the agency
It ends when the listing agreement expires
It ends unless the seller relists with the firm
It drops to limited confidentiality automatically
questions.why: Agency ends when the agreement expires, but confidentiality survives the ending. Students often assume every duty stops on the same day the agency does.

questions.q: A sales associate takes the listing on 2210 Fiddlewood Avenue for her employing broker. What kind of agent is the sales associate?
options: Special agent of the seller
Universal agent of the seller
Special agent of the broker
General agent of the broker
questions.why: A sales associate is a general agent of the employing broker, with ongoing authority in the broker's business. The listing broker is the seller's special agent, which is why "special agent of the seller" tempts.

questions.q: A broker takes one listing to sell a seller's house on Saw Palmetto Trail. What kind of agent is the broker to that seller?
options: General agent
Universal agent
Special agent
Designated agent
questions.why: The broker is hired for one specific task, and the authority ends when the task does, so the broker is a special agent. "General" tempts because the broker runs an ongoing business, but that is the associate's relationship to the broker.

questions.q: For years a property manager collects rent, signs leases and hires repairs for an owner of homes on Firewheel Road. What kind of agent is she?
options: General agent with ongoing authority
Special agent, since each lease is a separate task
Universal agent, because she handles many tasks
No agent at all, only a customer
questions.why: Ongoing authority across a continuing course of business makes her a general agent. Universal agency means authority to do essentially anything the principal could, like a broad power of attorney, which is rare in brokerage.

ch4-the-three-authorized-relationships-a.title: The three authorized relationships, and whose relationship it is

questions.q: One associate holds a single-agent listing on a house at 905 Firewheel Road. A colleague in the same office wants to be the buyer's single agent for that house. May she?
options: No, the firm already holds the seller's single agency
Yes, if both associates disclose it in writing
Yes, each associate holds their own relationship
Yes, if the broker approves it verbally
questions.why: The relationship is between the brokerage and the customer, so the whole firm is the seller's single agent. Treating each associate as a separate party to the relationship is the trap.

questions.q: A new licensee asks which relationships Florida authorizes between a licensee and a buyer or seller. Which list is accurate?
options: Single agent, dual agent and transaction broker
Seller's agent, buyer's agent and subagent
Single agent, disclosed dual agent and no brokerage relationship
Transaction broker, single agent and no brokerage relationship
questions.why: Florida allows exactly three: transaction broker, single agent and no brokerage relationship. Dual agency, disclosed or not, is not authorized, which is why lists containing it look familiar but are wrong.

questions.q: A sales associate works with a buyer on Spanish Stopper Drive. Who holds the relationship with the buyer, and who pays the associate?
options: The associate holds it; the buyer pays the associate
The brokerage holds it; the broker pays the associate
The associate holds it; the broker pays the associate
The brokerage holds it; the seller pays the associate directly
questions.why: Every relationship is between the brokerage and the customer, and the associate acts in the broker's name and is paid only by the broker. The options that look half right each get one of those two facts wrong.

questions.q: A licensee helps a buyer find and buy a home on Saw Palmetto Trail. No disclosure of any kind was ever signed. What relationship existed?
options: Transaction broker, by presumption
Single agent, implied from the work she did
No brokerage relationship, since nothing was signed
None, so the licensee acted unlawfully
questions.why: All licensees are presumed to be transaction brokers unless single agency or no brokerage relationship is established in writing. "Nothing signed" points to the default, not to no brokerage relationship, which itself needs a written notice.

questions.q: As transaction broker for both sides of 418 Saw Palmetto Trail, a licensee knows the seller privately would accept less than the list price. The buyer asks if the seller will take less. What should she do?
options: Tell him, since she represents both sides
Keep it confidential
Tell him only if the seller isn't present
Advise the seller to hold out for full price
questions.why: Limited confidentiality bars disclosing that the seller will accept less than the asking price. Advising the seller to hold out is also wrong, because a transaction broker advocates for neither side.

questions.q: A transaction broker knows the roof of a listed home leaks into the attic, which buyers can't see. The seller asks her to keep it quiet. What does she owe the buyer?
options: Silence, under limited confidentiality
Nothing, since she represents neither party fully
Disclosure only if the buyer asks about the roof
Disclosure of the leak
questions.why: Limited confidentiality covers price, terms and motive, never a known material fact about the property. Confusing limited confidentiality with limited honesty is the trap.

ch4-single-agent-and-its-nine-duties.title: Single agent and its nine duties

questions.q: A licensee is single agent for the seller of 1307 Spanish Stopper Drive. A touring buyer volunteers that he has sold his house and must close fast. What should she do with that fact?
options: Tell the seller, under full disclosure
Keep it private, since the buyer told her directly
Ignore it, since customers' statements don't matter
Share it only with the buyer's written permission
questions.why: The buyer is a customer, and the single agent owes her principal full disclosure, including what a customer lets slip. Confidentiality runs to the principal, not to the customer.

questions.q: A seller tells his single agent, "Don't mention the cracked slab." The crack can't be seen. What should the agent do?
options: Obey, since obedience is one of her duties
Stay quiet unless a buyer asks directly
Refuse, and withdraw if the seller insists
Keep it private under her duty of confidentiality
questions.why: Obedience covers lawful instructions only, and hiding a known material defect is not lawful. Confidentiality never covers a known defect, so the agent refuses and withdraws if the seller insists.

questions.q: A buyer's single agent learns that the seller of the home on Fiddlewood Avenue is her own relative. Which duty requires her to tell the buyer?
options: Loyalty
Obedience
Accounting for all funds
Full disclosure
questions.why: Full disclosure means telling the principal everything that bears on the deal, including the licensee's own interest, such as a relative on the other side. Loyalty is related but is about putting the principal first, not about telling him things.

ch4-consent-to-transition-to-transaction.title: Consent to transition to transaction broker

questions.q: A firm with a single-agent listing on 905 Firewheel Road acted as transaction broker for both sides for two weeks, then got the seller's written consent to transition. Does that cure the two weeks?
options: Yes, written consent applies back to the start
No, consent must be signed before the change
Yes, if the buyer signs it too
Yes, as long as the sale hasn't closed
questions.why: The principal's written consent must come before the change. Consent after the firm was already acting as transaction broker doesn't cure the period without it.

questions.q: A firm is single agent for the seller of 905 Firewheel Road. A buyer working with another associate in the office wants to offer. The seller never signed a consent to transition. What may the firm do?
options: Become transaction broker for both sides right away
Act as dual agent with both parties' consent
Get written consent first, or treat the buyer as a customer
Assign a designated sales associate to each party
questions.why: Without prior written consent the firm must get it before changing roles, or stay the seller's single agent and treat the buyer as a customer. Designated sales associates are nonresidential only, and dual agency is never allowed.

questions.q: A licensee has been a transaction broker for a buyer and now wants to become his single agent. What does that take?
options: Establishing single agency in writing through the single agent notice
A consent to transition signed by the buyer
Nothing, since the change is automatic
Written consent from the seller as well
questions.why: The reverse move needs no special consent form; single agency is always created in writing through the single agent notice. The consent to transition tempts, but it only governs moving from single agent to transaction broker.

questions.q: With a written no brokerage relationship notice, a licensee brings a buyer to a for-sale-by-owner home on Spanish Stopper Drive. She knows it floods, which isn't visible. What does she owe the buyer?
options: Nothing, because she represents no one
Silence unless the owner agrees to disclose
Disclosure only if she has an agreement with the owner
Disclosure of the flooding
questions.why: Even with no brokerage relationship, the licensee must disclose known facts that materially affect value and aren't readily observable. Reading "no brokerage relationship" as "no duties" is the trap.

questions.q: Which list states every duty a licensee owes with no brokerage relationship?
options: Honesty, limited confidentiality and accounting for funds
Loyalty, obedience and honesty
Honesty, accounting for funds and disclosing known hidden material defects
Honesty and skill, care and diligence only
questions.why: The three duties are honest dealing, accounting for funds, and disclosing known material facts not readily observable. Limited confidentiality tempts, but it belongs to the transaction broker list, not this one.

questions.q: A buyer tells a licensee who has no brokerage relationship with him his top price and asks her to keep it private. What confidentiality duty does she owe?
options: None; confidentiality isn't one of her duties
Limited confidentiality, like a transaction broker
Full confidentiality, like a single agent
Confidentiality only about his motivation
questions.why: No brokerage relationship carries no confidentiality of any kind. Students often import the transaction broker's limited confidentiality, which is a different relationship's list.

questions.q: The buyer and seller of a three-bedroom house on Fiddlewood Avenue both work with one firm. No single agency exists yet. Each wants an advocate. What can the firm lawfully offer both?
options: Transaction broker representation for both
Designated sales associates for each party
Disclosed dual agency with written consent
Separate single agents from the same office
questions.why: Designated sales associates are never available in a residential sale, so a firm working both sides can only be a transaction broker. Offering "designated sales associates" for a house is the trap answer.

questions.q: Two companies buying and selling a strip center want separate single agents from the same firm. Which condition must be met?
options: The broker assigns associates and tells the parties verbally
The property has four or fewer units
Each party requests it in writing and meets the statute's asset threshold
Both parties sign a dual agency consent
questions.why: Designated sales associates require a nonresidential deal, a written request from each party, and each party meeting the statutory asset threshold. Dual agency consent is never the route in Florida.

questions.q: In a nonresidential sale using designated sales associates, what duties does each associate owe the party assigned to them?
options: Transaction broker duties
No brokerage relationship duties
Only honesty and accounting for funds
Single agent duties
questions.why: Each designated sales associate has the duties of a single agent toward the assigned party. That is the point of the arrangement: each sophisticated party gets its own advocate inside one firm.

ch4-dual-agency-not-an-authorized-relati.title: Dual agency: not an authorized relationship

questions.q: The buyer and seller of a home on Saw Palmetto Trail both agree in writing to let one licensee be a full fiduciary for both. Under Florida law, what is true?
options: It's not permitted; the licensee should be a transaction broker
It's lawful only in a nonresidential sale
It's lawful because both consented in writing
It's lawful if the broker approves it
questions.why: Florida forbids dual agency whether disclosed or not, and consent doesn't fix it. Many other states allow disclosed dual agency, which makes the "both consented" answer feel right.

questions.q: Why does Florida forbid one licensee from being a fiduciary to both buyer and seller in the same deal?
options: Associates, unlike brokers, can't represent two parties
Loyalty can't push for the highest and lowest price at once
It would require two separate commissions
The buyer would lose the right to an inspection
questions.why: Loyalty to the seller means the highest price and loyalty to the buyer means the lowest, so one fiduciary can't owe both. Florida's answer is the transaction broker, who advocates for neither.

questions.q: A firm is single agent for the seller of 905 Firewheel Road, and an in-house buyer wants to offer. Both parties want the firm's help. What is the lawful route?
options: Disclosed dual agency signed by both parties
Designated sales associates for each side
Single agency for both, since it's one firm
Transaction broker, with the seller's prior written consent to transition
questions.why: The consent to transition exists so the firm can step down to transaction broker for both sides without ever becoming a dual agent. Designated sales associates are for nonresidential deals only.

questions.q: At an open house on Saw Palmetto Trail, a licensee hands out property sheets, then asks a visitor what he could really afford. What is the effect?
options: None; open houses are always exempt
The exemption is lost once she elicits confidential information
The exemption is lost only if a contract is signed
She automatically becomes the visitor's single agent
questions.why: The open house exemption covers only showings that don't involve eliciting confidential information, signing agreements or negotiating. Asking what he can really afford is eliciting confidential information, so the exemption is gone.

questions.q: Which of these is a residential sale under the Act's disclosure requirements?
options: A five-unit apartment building
A strip center
Agricultural property of 10 or fewer acres
Agricultural property of any size
questions.why: A residential sale includes agricultural property of 10 or fewer acres, along with property of four or fewer units. A five-unit building and a strip center fall outside the definition, though honesty still applies.

questions.q: A licensee arranges a lease of a house on Fiddlewood Avenue. When would the disclosure requirements apply to this lease?
options: When it includes an option to purchase the property
When the tenant asks for a written notice
When the landlord owns four or fewer units
When it is signed at an open house
questions.why: Rentals and leases are exempt unless an option to purchase all or part of the property is included. "Four or fewer units" tempts because it appears in the residential sale definition, but that definition covers sales.

ch4-when-the-notice-is-given-and-how-lon.title: When the notice is given, and how long it is kept

questions.q: A buyer's licensee shows a buyer the house on Spanish Stopper Drive on Saturday and plans to sign the representation agreement Monday. When was the single agent notice due?
options: At Monday's signing
Before any offer is written
At closing
Before Saturday's showing
questions.why: The notice is due before or at the representation agreement, or before showing property, whichever occurs first. The showing came first, so Monday was too late.

questions.q: A licensee will work with a buyer as a transaction broker. What written notice must she give before showing property?
options: A transaction broker notice
None, because transaction broker is presumed
A consent to transition
A no brokerage relationship notice
questions.why: Transaction broker is the presumed relationship and needs no written disclosure. The "transaction broker notice" looks familiar because older forms included one.

questions.q: A residential sale on Firewheel Road results in a written contract to purchase and sell. How long must the broker keep the brokerage relationship disclosure documents?
options: Until the transaction closes
Only while the listing is active
5 years
Until the buyer takes possession
questions.why: The broker keeps these documents for 5 years for residential transactions that result in a written contract. Closing feels like a natural end point, but the retention period runs well past it.

ch4-material-defects-what-every-licensee.title: Material defects: what every licensee owes the buyer

questions.q: A licensee knows a ceiling leak was painted over before listing. The buyer's inspection misses it. Must the licensee still disclose the leak?
options: Yes, the inspection doesn't cancel her duty
No, the inspection shifted the burden to the buyer
No, a painted-over leak is readily observable
Only if she is the buyer's single agent
questions.why: An inspection that missed a hidden defect doesn't cancel the licensee's duty to disclose what she knows. All three relationships owe this duty, so it doesn't depend on being a single agent.

questions.q: The seller of 2416 Fiddlewood Avenue hid storm flood damage under new flooring and listed "as is." A touring buyer asks nothing about water. What must the licensee do?
options: Nothing, since "as is" puts the risk on the buyer
Disclose only if the buyer asks about water
Disclose the flooding history
Stay quiet, since the seller's information is confidential
questions.why: The flooding is known, material and hidden, so it must be disclosed. Neither an "as is" clause nor the buyer's silence changes that, and confidentiality never covers a fact about the property.

questions.q: A licensee knows four things about a house on Spanish Stopper Drive. Which one most clearly must be disclosed to the buyer?
options: A ceiling stain visible from the hallway
A history of sinkhole activity
A dripping kitchen faucet
The seller's reason for moving
questions.why: A sinkhole history can materially affect value and isn't readily observable. The stain is observable, the faucet isn't material, and the seller's reason for moving is confidential.

questions.q: A broker runs the business from a spare bedroom on Sawgrass Court, meets clients at coffee shops, and has no registered office and no sign. What is the violation?
options: Running a brokerage out of a residence
Meeting clients away from the office
Having no registered office with a sign at the entrance
None, because a sign is required only for storefront offices
questions.why: A broker's office can be in a residence if local zoning allows it, but it must exist, be registered, and carry a sign readable from outside. The tempting answer blames working from home, which is allowed.

questions.q: A sales associate rents a small storefront, calls it her "desk," and puts her own name over the door. How does Florida treat this?
options: Allowed, if her broker approves the lease
A violation, because a sales associate may not maintain an office of her own
Allowed, if she registers the storefront in her own name
Allowed, as long as the broker's name appears somewhere inside
questions.why: The office exists so the public can find the person who is accountable, and a sales associate is never that person. Calling it a desk or getting the broker's blessing does not change that she is running her own office.

questions.q: Which entrance sign meets the Florida rule for a broker's office?
options: The sales associate's name in large letters, with the broker's name below it
The brokerage's trade name alone, with no other wording
A sign posted inside the lobby where only visitors can see it
The broker's name, trade name and "Licensed Real Estate Broker," with an associate's name below
questions.why: The sign must be readable from outside and carry the broker's name, any trade name, and words identifying a real estate business. An associate's name may appear, but only underneath the broker's, which is the trap in the first option.

questions.q: A broker opens a second location across town, staffs it with two sales associates, and does not register it because "it's the same company." What is the correct view?
options: It is a branch office and must be registered separately, with its own fee and sign
The main office registration covers every location of the same company
It needs registration only if a broker works there full time
It needs its own sign, but not its own registration
questions.why: Any additional location where the brokerage does business is a branch office, each registered separately with its own fee and sign. Being the same company is exactly why it is a branch, not a reason to skip registration.

questions.q: A broker places a trailer on a subdivision being sold, used for shade and signing contracts for that subdivision's lots only. Is it a branch office?
options: Yes, every location where contracts are signed is a branch office
No, but only if no sales associates ever work in it
No, as long as it is used only for that subdivision's sales and nothing else
No, because any temporary structure is exempt whatever happens there
questions.why: A temporary shelter on a subdivision is not a branch office if it serves only that subdivision's sales and nothing else is conducted from it. The exemption depends on how it is used, not on its being temporary.

questions.q: The same subdivision trailer starts taking listings on homes elsewhere in the county. What changes?
options: Nothing, because it still sits on the subdivision site
Nothing, because it is still a temporary structure
It now needs only a sign at the entrance
It loses the exemption and must be registered as a branch office
questions.why: The trailer is exempt only while it is used for that subdivision's sales and nothing else. Once other brokerage business is conducted there, it is an additional location doing business, which makes it a branch office.

questions.q: A yard-sign rider on Bayshore Lane shows a team name, "call" and a cell number, and nothing else. How does Florida treat it?
options: Allowed, because team names are permitted in advertising
A blind ad, because the brokerage's registered name is missing
Allowed, because the cell number lets the public reach a licensee
Allowed, as long as the broker approved the rider in advance
questions.why: Every ad must show the brokerage's registered name where a reader can see it; without it the ad is blind and prohibited. Team names are allowed, which is the trap, but only alongside the brokerage name, never instead of it.

questions.q: A sales associate runs a blind ad that her broker never saw or approved. Who is responsible for it?
options: Only the sales associate, since the broker never saw it
No one, if the ad is taken down once noticed
The broker, even though the broker never saw it
Only the team leader whose name appears in the ad
questions.why: The broker is responsible for every ad the brokerage or its associates run, even one the broker never saw. Not knowing about it feels like a defense, but it is not one.

questions.q: A sales associate posts a listing on her personal social media profile with her name and photo, linking to the brokerage's listing page. The post itself has no brokerage name. Is it compliant?
options: No, the brokerage name must appear on every page and point of contact, including the post
Yes, personal social media profiles are not advertising
Yes, because the linked listing page shows the brokerage name
Yes, because her own name identifies who is advertising
questions.why: On the internet the brokerage-name rule follows every page and every point of contact, including a social post or profile. Having the name one click away, or showing only the associate's name, does not cure the post.

questions.q: A buyer hands a sales associate a deposit on Friday evening. By when must the associate deliver it to the broker?
options: By the end of Saturday
By the end of Monday
Before leaving the office Friday evening
By the end of Wednesday
questions.why: The associate must deliver it by the end of the next business day, and the next business day after Friday is Monday. Saturday is the calendar-day answer the exam hopes you take.

questions.q: A sales associate receives a deposit Friday evening and gives it to the broker Monday. By when must the broker place it in the escrow account?
options: By the end of Monday
By the end of Tuesday
By the end of Wednesday
By the end of Thursday
questions.why: The broker has until the end of the third business day after the brokerage received it, and it was received Friday when the associate got it, so Wednesday. Thursday counts from the day it reached the broker's desk; Monday counts calendar days.

questions.q: A broker is choosing where to hold sales deposits. Which account is permitted?
options: The brokerage's operating account, tracked separately in the books
A separate escrow account at a bank in Georgia
The sales associate's personal account overnight, until the broker is available
A separate escrow account at a credit union located in Florida
questions.why: Deposits go into a separate escrow account at a bank, savings association, credit union or trust company located in Florida. An out-of-state bank fails the Florida requirement, and no deposit may sit in an operating or personal account even briefly.

questions.q: A broker short on payroll takes $4,000 from the escrow account on Tuesday and puts it all back on Friday. What is this?
options: Conversion, from the moment the money left the account
Commingling, the lesser offense, because it was repaid
No violation, because it was repaid within the week
Permitted, because it is under the $5,000 property-management cushion
questions.why: Using escrow money as your own is conversion, and intent to repay is not a defense. The $5,000 figure is a cushion of the broker's own money for bank charges, not a borrowing limit.

questions.q: A broker wants to keep some of the brokerage's own money in the sales escrow account to cover bank charges. What does Florida allow?
options: Up to $5,000
None at all
Up to $1,000
Any amount, as long as it is documented
questions.why: Florida allows up to $1,000 of the broker's own money in a sales escrow account. The $5,000 figure is the limit for a property-management escrow account, which is the number the exam swaps in.

questions.q: A broker keeps $4,000 of the brokerage's own money in a property-management escrow account to cover bank charges. How does Florida treat this?
options: Commingling, because no broker money may ever be in escrow
Permitted, because it is within the property-management limit
Commingling, because it is over the $1,000 limit
Conversion, because the broker controls the account
questions.why: Florida allows up to $5,000 of the broker's own money in a property-management escrow account to cover bank charges. The $1,000 limit applies to a sales escrow account, so applying it here is the mistake. ($4,000 is a scenario amount.)

questions.q: Every month a broker files the escrow bank statements in a binder, but never writes any comparison. Has the broker reconciled the accounts?
options: Yes, the bank statement shows the account balance
Yes, if the bank has certified the statements
Yes, if the broker reviews the binder once a quarter
No, the bank statement is not the reconciliation
questions.why: The reconciliation is the broker's own written comparison, prepared monthly, signed, dated and kept. Filing statements feels like recordkeeping, but a broker who never writes the comparison has not reconciled anything.

questions.q: Which document satisfies the monthly escrow reconciliation rule?
options: The bank's monthly statement for the escrow account
A ledger listing each deposit received that month
A written comparison of bank balance, outstanding items and total deposits, signed and dated
An unsigned spreadsheet the bookkeeper updates whenever a shortage appears
questions.why: The reconciliation compares the bank balance, the outstanding items and the total of all individual deposits, and the broker signs it, dates it and keeps it. A statement or a deposit list alone is only one side of the comparison.

questions.q: A broker's monthly reconciliation shows the escrow account holds more than the total of the individual deposits. What must the broker do?
options: Keep the extra as brokerage income
Explain the overage and correct it
Nothing, because only shortages need attention
Move the extra into the brokerage's operating account without explanation
questions.why: Shortages and overages both have to be explained and corrected. Treating an overage as harmless, or as the brokerage's money, is the tempting mistake.

questions.q: A buyer and seller on Heron Bay Drive both claim a deposit. The broker sends no notice, starts no procedure, and leaves it in escrow for a year. Later the seller turns out to be entitled. Is there a violation?
options: Yes, sitting on it without notice or a procedure is the violation
No, because the money stayed safely in escrow
No, because the rightful party is eventually paid
Only if the broker had a personal interest in the deal
questions.why: Doing nothing is the violation, regardless of who deserved the money. Keeping funds safely in the account feels responsible, but the broker must notify FREC and start an authorized settlement procedure.

questions.q: A broker receives the last of two conflicting demands for a deposit. When must the broker notify FREC in writing?
options: Within 15 calendar days of the first demand
Within 30 business days of the last demand
Only after the buyer and seller fail to settle on their own
Within 15 business days of the last demand
questions.why: Notice to FREC is due within 15 business days of the last demand. The 30 business days is the separate deadline to start one of the four settlement procedures, which is why it is the tempting wrong answer.

questions.q: A broker requests an escrow disbursement order from FREC, follows it, and is then sued by the party who did not get the deposit. What is the broker's position?
options: Liable, because the broker paid the losing party's money out
Protected, because FREC backs a broker who obeyed its order
Liable unless mediation was tried before the order
Protected only if the broker also filed for interpleader
questions.why: A broker who follows the escrow disbursement order is protected, because FREC backs a broker who obeyed its order. The lawsuit makes it feel risky, but the EDO is itself one of the four authorized procedures.

questions.q: At closing, a grateful seller hands the sales associate a personal thank-you check. What is the correct view?
options: Allowed, because a gift is not a commission
Allowed, if the associate tells the broker about it
A violation, because only the employing broker may pay a sales associate
Allowed, if the seller is not the associate's client
questions.why: Only the employing broker can pay a sales associate for brokerage work, so a seller's thank-you check is a violation. Calling it a gift or disclosing it does not change who is paying.

questions.q: A customer buys a rental list from a brokerage, does not find a rental within 30 days, and asks for a refund. What is the customer owed?
options: 75 percent of the fee
100 percent of the fee
Nothing, unless the contract promised a refund
Nothing, because the list was accurate
questions.why: A customer who does not find a rental within 30 days gets 75 percent of the fee back on request. The 100 percent refund is for a customer who finds the list was inaccurate, which is the number the exam swaps in.

questions.q: A brokerage closed a sale five years ago, and a lawsuit over that sale is still pending. The broker wants to shred the file. What should the broker do?
options: Shred it, because the five-year period has passed
Shred the contracts but keep the reconciliations
Send the file to FREC and shred the brokerage's copy
Keep the records, because pending litigation extends the period
questions.why: Brokerage records are kept for five years, or longer if litigation is pending. Five years having passed is the tempting answer, but the pending lawsuit means the records stay.

questions.q: A licensee disputes the facts and has a formal hearing before an administrative law judge. Who issues the final order?
options: The administrative law judge
FREC
The probable cause panel
The District Court of Appeal
questions.why: The administrative law judge issues only a recommended order. FREC issues the final order and can accept, reject or modify the recommended penalty.

questions.q: FREC concludes a licensee's violation warrants revocation. What does FREC need in order to revoke the license?
options: A circuit court order confirming the revocation
A ruling from a District Court of Appeal
Nothing more, since FREC revokes on its own authority
The licensee's written agreement to the revocation
questions.why: FREC revokes licenses on its own authority through its final order. Courts come in only if the licensee appeals.

questions.q: Which of these is a third-degree felony?
options: Failing to give a required brokerage relationship disclosure
Running an ad without the brokerage name
Failing to prepare a monthly escrow reconciliation
Operating without a license
questions.why: Operating without a license is the third-degree felony, while most license law violations are second-degree misdemeanors. Skipping a required disclosure is a license-law violation, not a crime by itself.

questions.q: A sales associate's employing broker has his license suspended. The associate did nothing wrong. What is the status of the associate's license?
options: Ineffective until she moves to a new broker
Void
Revoked along with the broker's
Involuntarily inactive
questions.why: An ineffective license exists but can't be used, and she can work again once she moves to a new broker. Void means the license never existed or has been revoked.

questions.q: Buyers in several separate transactions win uncollectible judgments against the same licensee. What is the most the Recovery Fund will pay in total on that licensee's account?
options: $50,000 for each claimant, with no total cap
Only the first claim filed is paid
questions.why: The fund pays up to $50,000 per transaction but no more than $150,000 total against any one licensee, no matter how many claims.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the seven protected classes under the federal Fair Housing Act?
options: Familial status
Religion
Marital status
Handicap
questions.why: The federal list is race, color, religion, national origin, sex, familial status and handicap. Local ordinances may add classes, but the federal list is the exam's list.

ch7-the-exemptions-and-why-race-is-never.title: The exemptions, and why race is never one

questions.q: An owner-occupant of a four-unit building rents units herself, with no broker and no ads, and turns away an applicant because of his race. Is this lawful?
options: No, because the 1866 Civil Rights Act bans race discrimination with no exemptions
Yes, because the Mrs. Murphy exemption covers her
Yes, because no licensee was involved
Only if she lives in the building full time
questions.why: The Mrs. Murphy exemption comes from the Fair Housing Act. The 1866 Act bans race discrimination in any property transaction and has no exemptions at all.

questions.q: A licensee shows a family with three children only homes near the elementary school, assuming that's what they'll want. What is this?
options: Good service, since it matches their likely needs
Blockbusting
Redlining
Steering on familial status
questions.why: Guiding buyers toward or away from areas based on a protected class is steering, and helpful intent is no defense. Familial status is a protected class.

questions.q: A renter believes she was turned away because of her religion. How long does she have to file a complaint with HUD?
options: Two years, the same as a federal lawsuit
One year
There is no deadline for a HUD complaint
Only until the unit is rented to someone else
questions.why: A HUD complaint must be filed within one year. Two years is the deadline for a civil action in federal court.

questions.q: A tenant with a disability asks his landlord to let him install grab bars in his apartment. Which law governs the request?
options: The Americans with Disabilities Act
The Civil Rights Act of 1866
The Fair Housing Act
Neither, because apartments are exempt
questions.why: Housing falls under fair housing, not the ADA. The ADA covers public accommodations and commercial facilities, such as a brokerage office or a store.

ch7-florida-residential-landlord-and-ten.title: Florida Residential Landlord and Tenant Act

questions.q: A tenant moves out and the landlord has no claim against the security deposit. How long does the landlord have to return it?
options: 15 days
30 days
Three days, not counting weekends and legal holidays
Seven days
questions.why: With no claim, the deposit goes back within 15 days. Thirty days is the deadline for written notice of intent to keep some or all of it.

ch7-land-sales-telemarketing-and-the-res.title: Land sales, telemarketing and the rest

questions.q: A licensee cold-calls the owner of a just-expired listing that was held by another brokerage. The owner's number is on the Do-Not-Call registry. What is the status of the call?
options: Allowed, because the property was recently listed for sale
Allowed, because the licensee was calling about a listing, not selling
Allowed, because expired listings are public information
A violation, because there is no existing business relationship
questions.why: The registry exception is an existing business relationship, and the old listing was with a different brokerage. Calling about a listing is not an exception.

ch8-real-property-personal-property-and-.title: Real property, personal property and fixtures

questions.q: A restaurant tenant installed a walk-in cooler for its business. The lease is ending. Who gets the cooler?
options: The tenant, who may remove it and must repair the damage
The landlord, because anything attached becomes real property
The landlord, unless the lease says the tenant keeps it
Whoever paid more toward the installation
questions.why: Equipment a commercial tenant installs for its business is a trade fixture and stays the tenant's personal property. The tenant can remove it before the lease ends, as long as it repairs the damage.

questions.q: An owner leases her duplex on Tamarind Avenue to a tenant. During the lease, what does she hold?
options: Nothing, until the tenant moves out
Only the right to collect rent
The bundle of rights minus possession
A life estate lasting the lease term
questions.why: A lease hands out one stick, possession, for a time. The landlord still owns the property and gets possession back when the lease ends.

questions.q: An owner's lot fronts a lake. Which term describes her water rights?
options: Riparian rights
Littoral rights
Appurtenant rights
Easement rights
questions.why: Lakes, seas and oceans carry littoral rights. Riparian rights belong to land along flowing water, a river or stream.

questions.q: A lot on Seagrape Circle is deeded to a church "on the condition that" it be used for worship. The church builds a parking lot on it. What happens?
options: Title reverts to the grantor's heirs automatically
The church keeps it, because the condition is unenforceable
The grantor's heirs have a right of re-entry and must act to take it back
The state takes title by escheat
questions.why: "On the condition that" creates a fee simple subject to a condition subsequent, which doesn't end on its own. Automatic reversion comes with "so long as" language, the determinable fee.

questions.q: A grantor deeds a house to Rosa for life, then to Rosa's nephew. What does the nephew hold?
options: A reversion
A life estate pur autre vie
A tenancy in common with Rosa
A remainder
questions.why: Property that passes to a third person named in the deed when a life estate ends is a remainder. A reversion is when it goes back to the original grantor.

questions.q: A lease on Mango Street runs from February 1 to July 31. What kind of tenancy is it?
options: Periodic tenancy
Estate for years
Tenancy at will
Tenancy at sufferance
questions.why: Definite beginning and end dates make it an estate for years, even though it lasts six months. It ends on its end date without notice.

ch8-forms-of-ownership-severalty-and-co-.title: Forms of ownership: severalty and co-ownership

questions.q: Alma and Teo, who are not married, take a deed "to Alma and Teo" with no other language. Teo dies. Who gets his share?
options: Alma, by right of survivorship
Alma, as tenant by the entireties
The state, by escheat
Teo's heirs or devisees
questions.why: Under section 689.15, a conveyance to two or more people is a tenancy in common unless it expressly provides for survivorship. A tenant in common's share passes to heirs or devisees.

ch8-ownership-by-business-entities-and-t.title: Ownership by business entities and trusts

questions.q: A house on Seagrape Circle is held in a Florida land trust. Who holds the rights to use and control it and to its income?
options: The beneficiaries
The trustee, as the title holder
The county, until the trust document is recorded
The original grantor
questions.why: In a land trust the trustee holds legal title, but the beneficiaries hold the rights to use, control and income. The public record shows only the trustee's name.

questions.q: A Florida resident's homestead sits on contiguous land outside a municipality. What does the 160-acre figure govern?
options: The land eligible for the $25,000 tax exemption
The cap on yearly Save Our Homes increases
The land protected from forced sale by most creditors
The land a spouse must approve before a sale
questions.why: The half-acre and 160-acre limits define how much land is protected from forced sale. The $25,000 exemption is a separate tax benefit.

questions.q: A buyer signs a contract for a resale condo on Mango Street. Under the current statute, how long does she have to cancel?
options: 15 days after the later of signing or receiving the documents
7 days, excluding weekends and legal holidays, after the later of the two
3 days after the later of the two
7 calendar days, weekends included, after the later of the two
questions.why: Section 718.503, as amended effective July 1, 2025, gives a resale buyer 7 days excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays. Fifteen days is the developer-sale period, and three is the old version.

questions.q: A buyer acquires shares in a corporation that owns a building, plus a proprietary lease on one unit. What does she own?
options: A cooperative interest
A condominium unit
A timeshare estate
A tenancy at will
questions.why: Stock plus a proprietary lease is a co-op. A condo owner holds fee simple title to the unit itself, with its own tax bill.

questions.q: A buyer off Seagrape Circle finds an extra assessment for roads and drainage on her property tax bill. What is its likely source?
options: The homeowners' association under Chapter 720
The condominium association
A Community Development District under Chapter 190
The county property appraiser's homestead office
questions.why: A CDD is a special-purpose local government that repays infrastructure bonds through assessments on the property tax bill. An HOA is a private corporation that enforces deed restrictions.

questions.q: A contract for a house in a mandatory HOA community doesn't reference the disclosure summary. The buyer receives it, closes, and two weeks later wants out. Can she void the contract?
options: Yes, because the 3 days start at closing
No, the right ended at closing
Yes, any time before her first assessment is due
Yes, because the summary came after she signed
questions.why: Under section 720.401 she could void within 3 days after receiving the summary or before closing, whichever came first. Closing ended the right.

questions.q: A buyer signs a timeshare contract at a resort on Tamarind Avenue on a Saturday and gets all required documents that day. When does her cancellation right end?
options: Midnight on the 10th business day after signing
15 days after signing
Midnight on the following Saturday
Midnight on the Tuesday ten days later
questions.why: Section 721.10 runs the right until midnight of the 10th calendar day, weekends included. Business days and a 15-day period belong to other rules.

questions.q: A seller on Banyan Terrace signs a deed, seals it in an envelope, and tells the buyer not to open it until the seller dies. Has title passed?
options: Yes, when the seller signed it
Yes, when the buyer took the envelope
No, the seller kept control, so there was no delivery
No, because the deed was not yet recorded
questions.why: Delivery means handing over the deed with intent to transfer, and this seller kept control. Recording isn't what passes title; delivery and acceptance do.

questions.q: A hurricane suddenly washes away part of a waterfront lot. Under Florida's general rule, what happens to the boundary?
options: It moves to the new waterline, by erosion
It stays where it was before the event
It moves to the new waterline, by reliction
The lost land escheats to the state
questions.why: Sudden loss is avulsion, and Florida generally leaves the boundary where it was before the event. Erosion is gradual and does move the boundary.

questions.q: A neighbor on Snook Creek Road has openly fenced and used part of the next lot for eight years, with no deed and no tax payments. What is the result?
options: He owns it, since the 7-year period has run
He gets a prescriptive easement instead
The claim fails without the tax payments
He owns it once he records a notice of his claim
questions.why: Without color of title, Florida requires a return filed with the property appraiser and the property taxes paid during the 7 years. Time alone isn't enough.

ch9-what-makes-a-florida-deed-valid.title: What makes a Florida deed valid

questions.q: A grantor signs a deed before a notary, and no witnesses sign. The grantee does not sign. Is the deed valid in Florida?
options: No, it lacks two subscribing witnesses
Yes, the notary's acknowledgment is enough
No, because the grantee never signed
Yes, once it is recorded
questions.why: Section 689.01 requires the grantor to sign in the presence of two subscribing witnesses. Acknowledgment is needed only to record, and the grantee never has to sign.

questions.q: Which part of a deed defines the estate being granted, such as fee simple or a life estate?
options: The granting clause
The testimonium clause
The exceptions and reservations
The habendum clause
questions.why: The habendum, "to have and to hold," defines the estate. The granting clause holds the words that transfer it.

questions.q: A buyer takes a bank-owned house on Ixora Drive by special warranty deed. A title defect from the owner before the bank surfaces. What protects the buyer?
options: The bank's warranty, since the bank is the seller
Title insurance, not the deed
The bank's covenant of further assurance
The foreclosure judgment against the prior owner
questions.why: A special warranty deed covers only defects that arose while the grantor owned the property. The earlier owner's defect falls outside it, so title insurance is the buyer's protection.

questions.q: A seller on Wild Coffee Lane sells to Buyer A, who moves in but never records. The seller then sells to Buyer B, who pays full price and records. Who has the better claim?
options: Buyer B, who recorded first
Buyer B, who paid full value
Neither, until a court divides the property
Buyer A, whose possession gave B notice
questions.why: Florida's notice statute protects only a later buyer who paid value without notice. A's possession charged B with notice, so A wins.

questions.q: A buyer on Snook Creek Road finances her purchase, and her lender requires a lender's title policy. Whom does that policy protect?
options: Only the lender, for the loan balance
The buyer and the lender equally
The buyer, for the purchase price
The seller, who gave the deed's warranties
questions.why: A lender's policy protects only the lender, and its coverage falls as the loan is paid down. The buyer needs her own owner's policy.

ch9-ownership-restrictions-the-governmen.title: Ownership restrictions: the government's four powers

questions.q: A county rezones a lot, which lowers its market value. Which power is this, and is compensation owed?
options: Eminent domain, and full compensation is owed
Police power, and no compensation is owed
Taxation, and the owner gets a tax credit
Escheat, and the state pays the difference
questions.why: Zoning is police power, and ordinary regulation owes no compensation. Compensation is owed only when government takes property through eminent domain.

questions.q: A homeowner on Banyan Terrace pays her general contractor in full. He never pays the cabinet supplier, who served its notice correctly. Can the supplier lien her house?
options: No, because she paid in full
No, only the general contractor can claim a lien
Yes, the supplier keeps its construction lien rights
Only if she signed a contract with the supplier
questions.why: Under Florida's construction lien law, a supplier that served its notice correctly keeps lien rights even after the owner pays the contractor. That's why owners collect lien releases before final payment.

questions.q: A neighbor on Ixora Drive has openly crossed the next lot to reach the canal, without permission, for 10 years. What does he have?
options: No easement yet, because Florida's prescriptive period is 20 years
A prescriptive easement
An easement by necessity
Ownership of the path he walks
questions.why: Florida's prescriptive period is 20 years, so 10 years of use isn't enough. Even after 20, he would get a right to use, not ownership.

questions.q: Zoning on Wild Coffee Lane allows duplexes, but the recorded subdivision covenants allow only single-family homes. Can an owner build a duplex?
options: Yes, because zoning overrides private covenants
No, because the more restrictive rule controls
Yes, if the county issues a building permit
Only after a quiet-title judgment
questions.why: When a deed restriction and a zoning ordinance conflict, the more restrictive one controls. Zoning permission doesn't override the single-family covenant.

ch10-why-a-street-address-is-not-enough.title: Why a street address is not enough

questions.q: Which of these is a legal description of a Florida parcel?
options: The street address, 2210 Spanish Moss Trail
The county parcel identification number
A description identifying one parcel with boundaries locatable on the ground
The owner's name and mailing address
questions.why: A legal description must identify one parcel only, with boundaries that can be located on the ground. A street address and a parcel ID do neither.

questions.q: How many square feet are in one acre?
questions.why: An acre is 43,560 square feet. 5,280 is the feet in a mile, a linear measure, and 640 is the acres in a section.

questions.q: A description on Osprey Ridge Road runs from "the southwest corner of Section 14, thence North 300 feet to the point of beginning." Where is the point of beginning?
