options: At the southwest corner of Section 14
At the center of Section 14
300 feet east of that corner
300 feet north of that corner
questions.why: The section corner is the point of commencement, where the measuring starts. The parcel's first corner, the point of beginning, is 300 feet north of it.

questions.q: Which principal meridian is the starting point for government survey descriptions in Florida?
options: A meridian passing through Miami
A federal meridian named for another state
The Tallahassee Meridian
The Florida-Georgia state line
questions.why: Florida's grid starts where the Tallahassee Meridian and its base line intersect, in Tallahassee. Every Florida township is located by counting from that point.

questions.q: How far apart are township lines?
options: 36 miles
24 miles
1 mile
6 miles
questions.why: Township lines run east–west every six miles. Thirty-six is the square miles in a township, and 24 miles is the spacing of the correction lines.

questions.q: Which section lies directly south of section 1 in a township?
options: Section 2
Section 7
Section 12
Section 6
questions.why: Section 1 is in the northeast corner, and the second row runs west to east from 7 to 12, putting 12 directly below 1. Section 7 sits under section 6, in the northwest.

questions.q: How many acres are in "the N 1/2 of the NE 1/4 and the SE 1/4 of the NE 1/4 of Section 22"?
options: 120 acres
80 acres
40 acres
20 acres
questions.why: "And" joins two separate pieces: the N 1/2 of the NE 1/4 is 80 acres and the SE 1/4 of the NE 1/4 is 40, for 120. Multiplying through the "and" would give a much smaller parcel.

questions.q: What is missing from "Lot 14, Block C, Silver Palm Estates, Broward County" that keeps it from being a reliable legal description?
options: The street address
The plat book and page where the plat is recorded
The parcel identification number
The owner's name
questions.why: Lot and block works by reference to the recorded plat, so the plat book and page tie it to one parcel. Without them, a similar subdivision name or a replat can leave it ambiguous.

questions.q: A condo unit on Magnolia Bend is legally described by reference to which recorded document?
options: The subdivision plat
The county tax roll
The building permit
The declaration of condominium
questions.why: The declaration and its attached survey set each unit's horizontal and vertical boundaries, so the description cites the recorded declaration. A plat is the reference for lot and block.

questions.q: A lot on Osprey Ridge Road is listed as "75 × 140." How many feet of frontage does it have?
options: 75 feet
140 feet
Whichever side is longer
None until a survey states it
questions.why: Front footage is always listed first, so the lot has 75 feet facing the road. The 140 feet is depth, which a front-foot price ignores.

ch11-what-a-contract-is-and-how-contract.title: What a contract is, and how contracts are classified

questions.q: Both parties signed a sales contract on Loquat Street last week. Closing is next month. How is the contract classified today?
options: Executed, because both parties have signed it
Executory, because performance is still pending
Unilateral, because only the seller is bound so far
Implied, because the deed has not been delivered
questions.why: Executed means fully performed by everyone, and closing hasn't happened yet. Signing alone leaves the contract executory.

questions.q: A buyer on Mangrove Bend signs a sales contract with the seller but gives no earnest money deposit. What is the status of the contract?
options: Void, because there is no consideration
Voidable by the seller until a deposit is paid
Valid, because the mutual promises are consideration
Unenforceable until a deposit reaches the escrow agent
questions.why: The exchange of promises is consideration, so the contract is valid without earnest money. The deposit shows seriousness and protects the seller; it doesn't create the deal.

questions.q: A seller on Hibiscus Avenue orally agrees with a buyer on price and closing date, then backs out. What is the oral agreement?
options: Void, because it was never a contract
Illegal, so both parties face penalties
Voidable at the buyer's option
Unenforceable under the statute of frauds
questions.why: A contract to sell land must be in writing to be enforced in court, but the oral deal isn't void or illegal. Had both sides closed voluntarily, nothing would be wrong with the sale.

ch11-offer-acceptance-and-when-the-contr.title: Offer, acceptance, and when the contract exists

questions.q: A seller on Firebush Court signs a buyer's offer but changes the closing date by one week and initials the change. What has the seller done?
options: Accepted the offer, with a minor amendment
Made a counteroffer that rejected the original offer
Created a contract effective on the seller's signature
Accepted the offer, subject to the buyer's later approval
questions.why: Acceptance must match the offer exactly, so any change to any term is a counteroffer. There is no contract until the buyer accepts the change and it is delivered back.

questions.q: An adult signs a contract with a 16-year-old on Poinsettia Drive. How is the contract classified?
options: Void, so neither party can enforce it
Voidable, at the option of either party
Voidable, at the option of the minor only
Unenforceable, so a court will not hear it
questions.why: A contract with a minor is voidable at the minor's option: the minor may keep it or cancel it. The adult has no right to cancel.

ch11-licensees-and-the-practice-of-law.title: Licensees and the practice of law

questions.q: A buyer on Loquat Street asks the sales associate to add a clause letting him cancel if his business deal falls through. What may she do?
options: Write the clause in the margin, since the buyer requested it
Draft the clause, as long as the seller initials it too
Use an approved pre-printed addendum or recommend an attorney
Explain the clause's legal effect and let the buyer write it
questions.why: Licensees may fill in approved standard forms but may not write custom legal clauses or give legal advice. When the forms don't cover it, the job is to recommend an attorney.

ch11-listing-agreements-and-buyer-broker.title: Listing agreements and buyer brokerage agreements

questions.q: A written listing on Mangrove Bend runs 90 days and then renews monthly until the seller cancels in writing. What is wrong with it?
options: Nothing, as long as the seller initialed the renewal clause
Nothing, because the 90-day term is a definite expiration date
It requires the seller to give notice after the expiration date
The renewal is valid only if the broker also signs it
questions.why: Florida forbids a listing provision requiring the owner to notify the broker of cancellation after the expiration date. An automatic renewal the owner must opt out of does exactly that.

ch11-the-sales-contract-the-florida-real.title: The sales contract: the Florida Realtors/Florida Bar forms

questions.q: Under the FR/BAR AS IS contract, a buyer on Hibiscus Avenue gets a clean inspection but changes his mind about the neighborhood. Can he cancel and recover his deposit?
options: Yes, if he cancels within the inspection period
No, because the inspection found no defects
Yes, at any time before closing
No, because an AS IS buyer has no cancellation right
questions.why: During the inspection period the AS IS buyer may cancel in his sole discretion and get the deposit back. Once the period ends, that right is gone.

questions.q: A seller on Firebush Court had the attic replaced after termite damage, repainted, and sells under an AS IS contract without mentioning it. What is true?
options: The AS IS clause relieves the seller of any duty to disclose
The seller had a duty to disclose the known, hidden, material defect
Disclosure is required only if the buyer asks about it directly
Only the licensee, not the seller, has a duty to disclose
questions.why: Under Johnson v. Davis, a residential seller must disclose known facts that materially affect value and aren't readily observable. AS IS protects against repair demands, not concealment.

ch11-options-and-rights-of-first-refusal.title: Options and rights of first refusal

questions.q: A tenant on Poinsettia Drive holds a right of first refusal, not an option. The owner hasn't received any offers. What can the tenant do?
options: Force a sale at the current market price
Exercise the right at any time during the lease
Buy at the price stated in the lease
Nothing until the owner receives an offer to match
questions.why: A right of first refusal only lets the holder match an offer the owner receives, if the owner decides to sell. Forcing a sale at a set price is what an option does.

questions.q: A buyer on Loquat Street is making installment payments under a contract for deed. What does he hold before the final payment?
options: Equitable title and possession
Nothing until the deed is delivered
Legal title, with the seller holding a lien
A leasehold interest only
questions.why: Under a contract for deed the buyer holds equitable title and possession while the seller keeps legal title. He owns more than nothing before the last payment.

questions.q: A buyer on Mangrove Bend assigns her sales contract to her cousin, who then fails to close. Who is liable?
options: Only the cousin, since the rights were assigned
The buyer, because an assignor remains liable
No one, because the assignment discharged the contract
Only the seller, for allowing the assignment
questions.why: With an assignment, the assignor stays liable if the assignee doesn't perform. Only a novation releases the original party.

questions.q: A buyer on Hibiscus Avenue defaults. The contract makes the $20,000 deposit liquidated damages, and the seller elects to keep it. What else may the seller recover?
options: Nothing more, because the deposit is the whole remedy
Actual damages above the deposit
Specific performance in addition to the deposit
The deposit plus the full loss on resale
questions.why: When the contract makes the deposit liquidated damages and the seller elects to keep it, that is the entire remedy. The seller can't also sue for the full loss.

questions.q: A buyer on Banyan Street finances most of the price with a bank loan. Under Florida law, who holds legal title after closing?
options: The bank, until the loan is paid off
A trustee, on behalf of the bank
The buyer, with the bank holding a lien
The buyer, until a default shifts title to the bank
questions.why: Florida is a lien-theory state, so the borrower keeps legal title and the lender holds a lien. Lender title until payoff is title theory; title shifting on default is intermediate theory.

questions.q: Which document creates the borrower's personal obligation to repay a home loan?
options: The mortgage
The promissory note
The deed
The satisfaction of mortgage
questions.why: The promissory note is the borrower's promise to repay and the evidence of the debt. The mortgage pledges the property as security for that promise.

questions.q: Daniela and Tomas live in her house on Ridgewood Avenue, their homestead. Both signed a mortgage on it, and they stop paying. Can the lender foreclose?
options: No, because homestead protects the home from forced sale
Yes, because homestead doesn't protect against a mortgage the owners signed
No, unless Tomas separately consents to the foreclosure
Yes, but only after the homestead status is removed
questions.why: Homestead protects a Florida home from most creditors, but not from a mortgage the owners voluntarily signed. That lender can foreclose.

questions.q: A borrower who is current on every payment sells her house, and the lender demands the full loan balance. Which clause allows that?
options: Acceleration clause
Defeasance clause
Escalation clause
Alienation clause
questions.why: The alienation, or due-on-sale, clause is triggered by a transfer of the property, even with no missed payments. Acceleration is triggered by default.

ch12-buying-a-property-that-already-has-.title: Buying a property that already has a mortgage

questions.q: The Okafors sell their house on Seagrape Drive to a buyer who assumes their loan, and the lender never releases them. The buyer defaults and the foreclosure sale falls short. Whom can the lender pursue?
options: Only the buyer, because he assumed the loan
Only the Okafors, as the original borrowers
No one, because the foreclosure sale settles the debt
The buyer, and then the Okafors
questions.why: An assuming buyer is personally liable, and the seller stays secondarily liable unless the lender releases them. A novation would have freed the Okafors.

questions.q: A homeowner paid off her mortgage, but the satisfaction was never recorded. What will the title search for her next sale show?
options: An open lien still on record
No lien, because the debt was paid
A lien assigned to a new holder
A lis pendens against the property
questions.why: Payment ends the debt, but the lien stays on the public record until the satisfaction is recorded. The title search will catch it as an open lien.

questions.q: A lender wants to foreclose on a house on Cypress Bend. Which describes the Florida process?
options: A trustee sells the property under a power of sale, without court
The lender sues, and the clerk holds a public sale after final judgment
The lender takes title automatically once the borrower defaults
The lender sells, then the borrower has a statutory right to buy it back
questions.why: Florida is a judicial foreclosure state: every residential foreclosure runs through circuit court and ends in the clerk's public sale. A trustee's sale without court is the nonjudicial method used in deed-of-trust states.

ch12-deficiency-judgments-deed-in-lieu-s.title: Deficiency judgments, deed in lieu, short sale

questions.q: A seller on Tamarind Road owes $310,000. The lender approves a $285,000 short sale, but the approval letter says nothing about the shortfall. What is true?
options: The short sale automatically cancels the $25,000 shortfall
The shortfall passes to the buyer at closing
The lender can still pursue the $25,000 shortfall
The lender must foreclose before it can recover anything
questions.why: A short sale ends personal liability for the shortfall only if the lender agrees in writing to waive it. Without that, the lender can still pursue it.

questions.q: A seller wants to give the buyer money toward the purchase, call it a gift, and keep it off the closing statement. What is this?
options: A permitted gift, since none of it goes to the licensee
Equity skimming, because the seller gives up equity
Mortgage fraud, because the money is hidden from the lender
A private matter between buyer and seller
questions.why: Any money that changes hands in the deal and is hidden from the lender is mortgage fraud, whatever it is called. The licensee must refuse to take part.

questions.q: A buyer closes on a loan to purchase her home on Banyan Street. The next day she wants out of the loan. What does TILA give her?
options: A three-business-day right of rescission
A three-business-day right, if she hasn't moved in yet
Rescission until the Closing Disclosure is recorded
No right of rescission on a purchase loan
questions.why: TILA's three-business-day rescission right covers certain refinances and home equity loans on a primary residence already owned. It never applies to the loan used to buy the home.

questions.q: In the early years of a graduated payment mortgage, the monthly payment doesn't cover the interest due. What happens to the loan balance?
options: It decreases slowly
It stays the same
It increases
It resets to the original amount
questions.why: The unpaid interest is added to the balance, which is negative amortization. The borrower ends up owing more than they borrowed.

questions.q: A buyer on Pelican Point Road has an ARM with a 2.5 percent margin. At adjustment the index rises from 4.25 to 5 percent. What is the new rate, before caps?
options: 6.75 percent
7.5 percent
5 percent
4.25 percent
questions.why: The rate is index plus margin, so 5 plus 2.5 is 7.5 percent. The margin stays fixed; only the index moved.

ch13-conventional-loans-and-private-mort.title: Conventional loans and private mortgage insurance

questions.q: A buyer on Royal Poinciana Drive puts 10 percent down on a conventional loan and pays PMI. Whom does the PMI protect?
options: The buyer, if she loses her job
The buyer's heirs, by paying off the loan at her death
The lender, against loss on default
The seller, until the sale closes
questions.why: PMI protects the lender against loss if the borrower defaults. Coverage for job loss or death describes credit life or mortgage life insurance.

questions.q: A buyer on Osprey Lane gets an FHA loan for a townhouse. What is FHA's role in the loan?
options: It insures the loan made by an approved lender
It lends the money directly to the buyer
It guarantees a portion of the loan
It buys the loan on the secondary market
questions.why: FHA doesn't lend; it insures loans made by approved lenders, so the lender is repaid on default. Guaranteeing a portion of the loan is what VA does.

questions.q: A veteran on Lantana Avenue sells to a civilian who assumes his VA loan. The VA does not release him. What is his position?
options: He's free of the loan, because the guaranty protects him
He's liable only for the funding fee
His entitlement is restored once the buyer assumes
He's still liable, and his entitlement stays tied up
questions.why: The VA guaranty protects the lender, not the veteran. Without a release of liability he stays liable, and his entitlement stays committed unless a qualified veteran buyer substitutes theirs.

questions.q: A buyer finances her home purchase with a loan from a commercial bank. Is that a purchase-money mortgage?
options: Yes, because it finances the purchase itself
No, because only seller financing is purchase-money
No, because a bank loan is a conventional mortgage instead
Yes, but only if the seller also carries a note
questions.why: A purchase-money mortgage is any mortgage given to finance buying the property. The phrase describes what the money buys, not who lends it.

questions.q: A buyer finances a condo sold furnished, with appliances and furniture, under a single mortgage. What type of mortgage is it?
options: Blanket mortgage
Wraparound mortgage
Open-end mortgage
Package mortgage
questions.why: A package mortgage covers real and personal property together. A blanket mortgage covers two or more parcels.

questions.q: Which primary-market participant brings borrower and lender together for a fee but does not lend?
options: Mortgage banker
Mortgage broker
Savings association
Credit union
questions.why: A mortgage broker arranges loans and is paid for arranging. A mortgage banker lends its own or borrowed money and often services the loan.

questions.q: What does Ginnie Mae do in the secondary mortgage market?
options: Buys conventional loans from savings associations
Insures loans made by approved lenders
Guarantees securities backed by FHA and VA loans
Packages conventional loans into securities it sells
questions.why: Ginnie Mae, part of HUD, guarantees securities backed by pools of FHA and VA loans. It does not buy loans; buying conventional loans is Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac's role.

questions.q: A buyer on Pelican Point Road earns $8,000 a month gross and has $600 in other monthly debts. Using 28 and 36 percent, what is her maximum PITI?
options: $2,280, from the total obligations ratio
$2,240, from the housing expense ratio
$2,880, the total debt limit
Whichever of the two results is higher
questions.why: Both ratios use gross income, and the lower result governs. The housing ratio gives $2,240, below the $2,280 back-end limit.

questions.q: A buyer on Osprey Lane borrows $300,000 to buy a $375,000 house and pays 2 discount points. What do the points cost?
questions.why: A point is 1 percent of the loan amount, so 2 points on $300,000 is $6,000. Figuring them on the $375,000 price gives the wrong $7,500.

questions.q: A sales associate on Gumbo Limbo Lane received $5,400, which was 60 percent of what her broker received. What did the broker receive?
questions.why: The broker's amount is the total, so Total = Part ÷ Rate: $5,400 ÷ 0.60 = $9,000. Multiplying instead, or dividing by 0.06, are the classic slips.

questions.q: A lot on Ibis Court measures 150 by 290.4 feet and is priced at $700 per front foot. What is the price?
questions.why: The first number is customarily the frontage, so 150 × $700 = $105,000. Using the depth, or pricing the lot by the square foot, gives a different number.

questions.q: A seller wants to net $200,000 after paying a 6 percent commission. What must the property sell for?
questions.why: The net is 94 percent of the price, so $200,000 ÷ 0.94 = $212,765.96. Adding 6 percent to the net fails because commission is figured on the price.

questions.q: A house on Seminole Trail sells for $385,000 and appraises at $375,000. The lender lends 80 percent. What is the buyer's down payment?
questions.why: The lender uses the lower $375,000, so the loan is $300,000, and the buyer still owes the $385,000 price: $85,000 down. $77,000 wrongly applies 80 percent to the price.

questions.q: Renata borrows $308,000 at 6.5 percent with a monthly payment of $1,946.77. How much of her first payment goes to principal?
questions.why: Month 1 interest is $308,000 × 0.065 ÷ 12 = $1,668.33, and the rest of the payment is principal: $1,946.77 − $1,668.33 = $278.44.

ch14-florida-documentary-stamp-tax-on-de.title: Florida documentary stamp tax on deeds

questions.q: A single-family house in Orange County sells for $385,000, financed with a new $308,000 loan. What are the documentary stamps on the deed?
questions.why: Deed stamps go on the price: 3,850 × $0.70 = $2,695. $2,156 puts the deed rate on the loan, and $2,310 uses the Miami-Dade rate.

ch14-florida-documentary-stamp-tax-on-no.title: Florida documentary stamp tax on notes

questions.q: Renata signs a $308,000 note to buy a $385,000 house. What are the documentary stamps on the note?
questions.why: Note stamps go on the note amount: 3,080 × $0.35 = $1,078. $1,347.50 puts the note rate on the price, and $616 is the intangible tax.

questions.q: A buyer assumes the seller's existing mortgage instead of taking a new loan. What intangible tax is due on the assumed mortgage?
options: 2 mills on the assumed balance
2 mills on the full price
None, because it was taxed when originally recorded
$0.35 per $100 of the assumed balance
questions.why: The intangible tax applies only to new mortgages. An assumed mortgage was taxed when first recorded, so it isn't taxed again.

questions.q: A Florida closing is set for June 15, and this year's property taxes haven't been paid. How is the tax proration entered?
options: Credit seller, debit buyer
Debit seller, credit buyer
Debit both buyer and seller
Not prorated; the buyer pays the November bill
questions.why: The bill is unpaid and the seller owned part of the year, so the seller owes the buyer. The buyer then pays the full bill in November with the seller's money.

questions.q: Annual taxes of $4,745 are unpaid at a June 15, 2026 closing. Using the 365-day method, what is the seller's share?
questions.why: $4,745 ÷ 365 = $13.00 a day, and the seller owns January 1 through June 14, which is 165 days: $2,145. Counting June 15 for the seller adds a day too many.

questions.q: Annual taxes of $4,745 are unpaid at a June 15 closing. The question says to use 30-day months. What is the seller's share?
questions.why: Five months at $395.4167 is $1,977.08, plus 14 days at $13.1806 is $184.53, for $2,161.61. $2,145 is the 365-day answer, the usual decoy.

questions.q: A rented condo on Live Oak Boulevard closes June 15. The seller collected June's $2,400 rent on June 1. What is the rent proration?
options: Debit seller $1,280, credit buyer $1,280
Debit buyer $1,280, credit seller $1,280
Debit seller $1,200, credit buyer $1,200
Debit seller $1,120, credit buyer $1,120
questions.why: The buyer owns June 15 through 30, which is 16 days at $80, or $1,280. The seller is holding that rent, so the seller is debited and the buyer credited.

questions.q: How is the buyer's $20,000 deposit entered on the closing statement?
options: Credit seller, debit buyer
Credit buyer, debit seller
Credit buyer only
Credit seller only
questions.why: The deposit is already in escrow and counts toward what the buyer owes, so it is a single credit to the buyer. The seller's credit for it is already inside the full price.

questions.q: Who may act as closing agent on a Florida residential sale?
options: Only a Florida-licensed attorney
A title company or a real estate attorney
Only the listing broker
Only the lender's loan officer
questions.why: Florida residential closings are usually handled by a title company or a real estate attorney, and there is no requirement that an attorney conduct the closing. An attorney-only answer is the generic assumption the exam targets.

ch15-what-a-market-is-and-why-real-estat.title: What a market is, and why real estate's is different

questions.q: Which best describes the real estate market?
options: Efficient and national, like a stock exchange
Uniform, with prices that adjust in seconds
Local, with imperfect information
National, because most transactions are financed
questions.why: A house cannot move to where the buyers are, so markets are local, and every property differs, so information is imperfect. Efficient and national describe a stock exchange.

questions.q: Near Sabal Palm Avenue, listings fall from 180 to 90 while 30 homes still sell each month. What does this indicate?
options: A shift toward a seller's market
A shift toward a buyer's market
Demand fell because prices rose
Supply became elastic in the short run
questions.why: Months of inventory drops from 6 to 3, and fewer months means a tighter, seller-leaning market. Prices follow supply and demand, not the other way around.

questions.q: A county lengthens its permitting timelines and tightens building codes. What is the most likely effect on the market?
options: Demand falls
Supply rises
No effect, since regulation is not a market factor
Supply falls
questions.why: Government regulation is a supply factor even though it produces nothing. Slower permits and stricter codes mean less gets built.

questions.q: Construction loan rates rise sharply for homebuilders. In the textbook's framing, which factor is this?
options: A demand factor, through buyer affordability
A supply factor, through builders' costs
An economic characteristic called area preference
Neither, because rates are set by policy
questions.why: The question is about builders, and for builders interest rates are a supply factor because they set the cost of construction loans. For buyers, rates would be a demand factor.

questions.q: Identical houses on Flamingo Road and near the interstate sell far apart because buyers prefer the waterfront block. Which characteristic is this?
options: Immobility
Nonhomogeneity
Area preference
Indestructibility
questions.why: The price gap comes from people's preference for one location, which is area preference, an economic characteristic. Immobility is the physical fact that land can't move.

questions.q: Which of these is a physical characteristic of real estate?
options: Scarcity
Area preference
Permanence of investment
Nonhomogeneity
questions.why: Nonhomogeneity, or uniqueness, describes the land itself, so it is physical. Scarcity, area preference and permanence of investment are on the economic list.

ch15-business-cycles-and-real-estate-cyc.title: Business cycles and real estate cycles

questions.q: In the textbook's framing, how do real estate cycles relate to general business cycles?
options: They lead them
They tend to be longer and lag them
They move in lockstep with them
They repeat within each year
questions.why: Because construction takes years, real estate keeps building past the peak and responds late. Repeating within a year describes seasonal variation, not a cycle.

questions.q: Which indicator would best predict future housing supply in a county?
options: Closed sales last quarter
Average days on market
Building permits issued
Foreclosure levels
questions.why: Building permits are a leading indicator of supply to come. Closed sales report what already happened.

questions.q: A developer wants to know whether a specific site on Loxahatchee Drive, at its land cost and construction budget, will earn an acceptable return. What does she need?
options: A feasibility study
A market study
A comparative market analysis
A months-of-inventory count
questions.why: Testing one project's financial success at one site is a feasibility study. A market study only describes supply and demand for a property type in an area.

ch15-from-market-analysis-to-pricing-one.title: From market analysis to pricing one property

questions.q: A sales associate prepares a thorough CMA for a house on Sabal Palm Avenue and titles it "Appraisal." What is the problem?
options: None, as long as the analysis is accurate
Licensees may not prepare CMAs at all
Licensees may never be paid for a price opinion
Calling it an appraisal is the violation
questions.why: Florida allows licensees to prepare CMAs and price opinions, but not to refer to them as appraisals. Good analysis doesn't cure the wrong label.

questions.q: A lender wants to pay a Florida sales associate for a broker price opinion. Which is true?
options: Only a certified appraiser may accept the fee
The associate may be paid, through the employing broker
Once a fee is paid, the BPO becomes an appraisal
The lender must pay the associate directly
questions.why: Florida lets licensees provide valuation services for compensation, paid through the employing broker, as long as the work isn't called an appraisal.

questions.q: A seller sells her house to her brother for well under what similar homes bring. What does that sale price represent?
options: Market value, because a sale occurred
Cost
A market price, but likely not market value
Investment value
questions.why: The price is what actually happened, but a sale between relatives isn't arm's-length, so it is weak evidence of market value.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four characteristics of value?
options: Cost
Utility
Transferability
Scarcity
questions.why: The four are demand, utility, scarcity and transferability. Cost can be high while value stays low if no one wants the thing.

questions.q: A city changes the zoning on a neighborhood's lots. Which force affecting value is this?
options: Physical
Economic
Political
Social
questions.why: Zoning comes from government, which makes it a political force even though it concerns land.

questions.q: Two lots on Lignumvitae Street worth $150,000 each are combined into one parcel worth $360,000. What is the $60,000 increase?
options: Plottage value
Assemblage
Progression
Contribution
questions.why: Plottage is the increment in value from combining parcels. Assemblage is only the act of combining them.

questions.q: On an owner-occupied home, an appraiser's approaches give $410,000, $425,000 and $395,000. How does she reach her final opinion?
options: Averages the three
Weighs them, usually favoring sales comparison
Takes the highest figure
Weighs them, usually favoring the income approach
questions.why: Reconciliation weighs each approach by its reliability for the property type, and for an owner-occupied house sales comparison usually carries the most weight. Averaging is the decoy.

questions.q: The subject at 2214 Lignumvitae Street has no pool. Comp A, otherwise the same, sold for $430,000 and has a pool worth $20,000. What is Comp A's adjusted price?
questions.why: The comp is better than the subject by a pool, so subtract: $430,000 − $20,000 = $410,000. Adding the pool value moves the wrong way.

questions.q: At 618 Mahogany Drive the building costs $360,000 new and is 20 percent depreciated. The land is worth $90,000. What is the value by the cost approach?
questions.why: Depreciate only the building, $360,000 − $72,000 = $288,000, then add the land: $378,000. Depreciating land and building together gives the $360,000 decoy.

questions.q: At 3307 Lignumvitae Street, effective gross income is $139,200, operating expenses are $48,000 and the owner pays $62,000 a year on the mortgage. At an 8 percent cap rate, what is the value?
questions.why: NOI is $139,200 − $48,000 = $91,200, and $91,200 ÷ 0.08 = $1,140,000. The mortgage is personal to the owner, so subtracting it gives the $365,000 decoy.

ch16-gross-rent-and-gross-income-multipl.title: Gross rent and gross income multipliers

questions.q: A rented house at 2850 Mahogany Drive brings $2,400 a month, and comparable houses show a GRM of 150. What is the indicated value?
questions.why: A GRM applies to monthly rent: 150 × $2,400 = $360,000. Applying it to a year of rent produces the $4,320,000 decoy.

questions.q: In reconciling the value of a new special-purpose building, which approach usually carries the most weight?
options: Sales comparison
Income
An average of all three
Cost
questions.why: New or special-purpose buildings lean on the cost approach. An answer that averages the approaches is always wrong.

questions.q: A seller at 1509 Mahogany Drive insists on listing at $520,000, above what the comps support. What may the licensee do?
options: Refuse to list above the CMA's range
Adjust the CMA's comps to support $520,000
List at $520,000 with an accurate CMA
Call the CMA an appraisal to persuade the seller
questions.why: The seller decides the list price, so the licensee may list at $520,000. Falsifying the comps to support it would be misrepresentation.

questions.q: An analyst computing NOI for the fourplex at 1830 Coontie Avenue adds the value growth she expects this year. What's wrong with that?
options: Nothing, because appreciation is part of NOI
Appreciation is a hoped-for benefit, not part of the cash-flow calculation
Appreciation should be subtracted from NOI instead
Appreciation counts toward NOI only after the loan is paid off
questions.why: Appreciation is an expected benefit, not a guaranteed one, so it stays out of NOI. NOI comes from income and operating expenses only.

ch17-the-investor-s-four-concerns-risk-r.title: The investor's four concerns: risk, return, liquidity, management

questions.q: Why is real estate described as illiquid?
options: It requires active management
There is never a buyer at any price
It can't be turned into cash quickly without a significant loss
Its value doesn't keep pace with inflation
questions.why: Liquidity is how fast an asset converts to cash without a big loss, and selling a building takes months. Management is a separate concern.

ch17-advantages-and-disadvantages-of-rea.title: Advantages and disadvantages of real estate investment

questions.q: Which advantage of real estate investment can also become a risk?
options: Control
Tax shelter
Equity buildup
Leverage
questions.why: Leverage magnifies losses as well as gains, so some questions put it on both lists. The other three don't cut both ways like that.

questions.q: Raw land on Wild Lime Way is held until the area develops. What cash flow does it produce?
options: Positive, because appreciation counts as income
Negative, because taxes still come due
Zero, because carrying costs don't count
Positive, once the owner lists it for sale
questions.why: Vacant land earns no income but still carries taxes and insurance, so its cash flow is negative. Its only return is appreciation.

questions.q: A limited partner in an apartment syndication starts choosing tenants and approving repairs. What is the risk?
options: She can lose the protection of limited liability
None, because her liability is fixed by her investment
The partnership is converted into a REIT
Her share of income becomes taxed twice
questions.why: Limited liability depends on staying passive. A limited partner who takes control of management can lose it.

questions.q: At 1830 Coontie Avenue, NOI is $49,000, debt service is $36,000, and the investor put $150,000 down on a $600,000 price. What is the cash-on-cash return?
options: 25 percent
About 8.17 percent
5 percent
About 8.67 percent
questions.why: Cash-on-cash is the $13,000 cash flow over the $150,000 the investor put in. About 8.17 percent is the cap rate, NOI over price.

questions.q: When does borrowing raise an investor's return on cash invested?
options: Whenever the loan covers most of the price
Whenever property values are rising
When the property's return is higher than the cost of borrowing
When the loan carries a fixed interest rate
questions.why: Positive leverage needs the property to out-earn the debt. When the loan costs more than the property returns, leverage turns negative.

questions.q: Which figure goes on the bottom of the ROI calculation?
options: The property's current market value
The sale price after selling costs
The original loan balance
The amount the investor put in, including cash added later
questions.why: ROI is net return divided by what the investor invested. Value, price and loan balance all mix in money that isn't the investor's.

ch17-investment-analysis-what-a-licensee.title: Investment analysis: what a licensee may and may not do

questions.q: A licensee forwards a seller's 9 percent pro forma cap rate on a Coontie Avenue listing as actual income. Who has misrepresented?
options: Only the seller, who prepared the figure
The licensee who passed it on
No one, since projections are opinions
Only the employing broker
questions.why: Passing along projected rents as actual income, without saying so, is misrepresentation by the licensee who did it. Forwarding someone else's figure is no defense.

questions.q: Someone is paid a fee to find a buyer for a Florida dry-cleaning business. No real property is included. What license is required?
options: None, since no real estate changes hands
A separate Florida business broker license
A real estate license
A securities license only
questions.why: Florida's broker definition covers business opportunities whether or not real property is part of the sale. There is no separate business broker license.

ch17-what-is-being-sold-in-a-business-sa.title: What is being sold in a business sale

questions.q: In the café sale at 2210 Wild Lime Way, how is the kitchen equipment transferred?
options: By bill of sale
By warranty deed
By assignment
By quitclaim deed
questions.why: Equipment, furniture and inventory are personal property, which moves by bill of sale, not a deed. Assignment is how the lease moves.

questions.q: A buyer wants to avoid a business's unknown past liabilities. Which structure fits?
options: A stock sale
A sale of LLC membership interests
An asset sale
Either, since old debts never transfer
questions.why: In an asset sale the buyer usually takes on only the debts it agrees to. A stock or membership-interest sale buys the entity, debts included.

questions.q: The owner of a dry cleaner works there full-time and takes no salary. Before capitalizing income, what should the analyst do?
options: Use the reported profit as it stands
Capitalize gross revenue instead of profit
Lower the capitalization rate to compensate
Subtract a fair salary for the owner's work
questions.why: Reported profit with no owner salary overstates what a buyer would earn. The owner's salary comes out before capitalizing.

ch17-licensee-duties-in-a-business-sale.title: Licensee duties in a business sale

questions.q: A buyer hands a sales associate a deposit on a business purchase. How must it be handled?
options: As an escrow deposit, on the usual deadlines
Paid straight to the seller, since no house is involved
Held by the associate personally until closing
Exempt from escrow rules once a nondisclosure agreement is signed
questions.why: A deposit in a business sale is an escrow deposit in a brokerage transaction. The same deadlines apply as for any other deposit.

questions.q: A Satinwood Terrace owner's value is unchanged, but her tax went up. Who set the rate that caused it?
options: The property appraiser
The tax collector
The value adjustment board
The taxing authorities
questions.why: Each taxing authority sets its own millage through a budget process. The appraiser only sets value, and the collector only bills and collects.

ch18-ad-valorem-tax-and-the-january-1-da.title: Ad valorem tax and the January 1 date

questions.q: A Florida sale closes midyear, before this year's tax bill goes out. Who owes whom a credit for the tax?
options: The buyer owes the seller, since taxes were paid in advance
The seller owes the buyer
No one, because the lien attaches only when the bill is sent
The tax collector owes the seller a refund
questions.why: Florida property tax is paid in arrears, so the seller used part of the year without paying for it. The seller credits the buyer.

ch18-just-value-assessed-value-taxable-v.title: Just value, assessed value, taxable value

questions.q: Which value is the millage rate applied to?
options: Just value
Assessed value
Taxable value
The most recent sale price
questions.why: Taxable value is assessed value minus exemptions, and that's the number the rate multiplies. Just value comes first, before any cap or exemption.

questions.q: A tax rate of 20 mills equals what percentage of taxable value?
options: 2 percent
20 percent
One percent
One-tenth of one percent
questions.why: A mill is one-tenth of one percent, so 20 mills is 2 percent. Reading a mill as a full percent gives 20, the trap answer.

questions.q: Which taxes does the second homestead exemption reduce?
options: All taxes, including school taxes
School taxes only
Non-school taxes only
Special assessments only
questions.why: The second exemption covers assessed value between $50,000 and $75,000 and never applies to school taxes. Only the first $25,000 is exempt from everything.

questions.q: A buyer of a Sea Oats Road homestead is budgeting from the seller's current tax bill. What should the licensee explain?
options: The seller's cap transfers to her automatically
Assessed value resets to just value on the January 1 after the sale
Her assessed value can't rise more than 10 percent
Taxes are frozen for her first year of ownership
questions.why: The Save Our Homes cap doesn't transfer to a buyer; the property is reassessed at just value the next January 1. The 10 percent cap is for non-homestead property.

questions.q: An owner with a $180,000 Save Our Homes benefit sells and buys a new Florida homestead. Who gets the benefit?
options: The buyer of her old house
No one, because it ends at the sale
The owner, applied to her new homestead
It is split between her and her buyer
questions.why: Portability belongs to the owner and moves with her to her next Florida homestead. The buyer of the old house gets nothing.

questions.q: A homeowner receives a Notice of Proposed Property Taxes in August. What is it?
options: The tax bill, due on receipt
A delinquency notice from the tax collector
An offer of a tax certificate
The TRIM notice, a chance to object before rates are final
questions.why: The TRIM notice comes from the property appraiser in August and is not a bill. The tax collector sends the actual bill in the fall.

ch18-paying-the-bill-the-discount-schedu.title: Paying the bill: the discount schedule

questions.q: The 1720 Satinwood Terrace owner pays her $4,650 bill on March 31. What happens?
options: She pays $4,650 and is on time
She owes a delinquency penalty
She gets a 1 percent discount
A tax certificate is sold on her parcel
questions.why: March payments get no discount but are not late. Delinquency starts April 1.

questions.q: An investor wins the tax certificate on 1155 Sea Oats Road at 6 percent. What does she hold?
options: Title to the property
A tax deed, effective immediately
A right to collect rent from the owner
A lien that earns interest when the owner redeems
questions.why: A certificate is a lien, not ownership. Title changes only through a tax deed sale.

questions.q: A homestead owner on Satinwood Terrace gets a $12,000 sewer assessment. How does her homestead exemption affect it?
options: It cuts the charge by the exemption amount
It exempts homestead owners entirely
It doesn't reduce it at all
It reduces only the non-school share
questions.why: Homestead exemptions reduce ad valorem tax only. A special assessment is based on benefit, and the owner pays all of it.

questions.q: A homeowner sells her principal residence on Sea Oats Road at a loss. What can she deduct?
options: Nothing
The full loss
Up to $250,000 of the loss
Only the commission she paid
questions.why: A loss on a personal residence isn't deductible. Losses are deductible only on investment or business property.

questions.q: An investor completes a qualified 1031 exchange and takes no cash out. What happens to her gain?
options: It is permanently forgiven
It is deferred and carried into the new property's basis
It is taxed as ordinary income now
It is excluded like a home-sale gain
questions.why: A 1031 exchange defers the gain by carrying the old basis into the replacement property. The tax comes due on a later taxable sale.

questions.q: A seller finances a sale with a $100,000 gain and uses installment reporting. What does that change?
options: When the gain is reported
The total amount of gain
Whether the gain is taxable at all
The seller's basis in the property
questions.why: The gain is reported in proportion to payments received each year. The total gain stays the same.

questions.q: A county rezones a Slash Pine Road parcel from commercial to residential, halving its value. Is the owner owed compensation?
options: Yes, because the government must pay just compensation
Yes, for the value lost
Only if the owner bought before the rezoning
No, a value loss from regulation alone isn't compensable
questions.why: Zoning is police power, which regulates without compensation. Only a regulation leaving no economically viable use becomes a taking.

questions.q: How does zoning relate to a Florida local comprehensive plan?
options: Zoning carries out the plan and must be consistent with it
Zoning is the same thing as the plan
The plan is advisory, so zoning controls
The state writes zoning, and cities write the plan
questions.why: The plan is the long-range blueprint and comes first. Zoning carries it out, and a decision that contradicts the plan can be challenged.

questions.q: The developer of a new Spoonbill Point Drive subdivision pays a one-time charge to fund added sewer capacity. What is it?
options: A special assessment
An ad valorem tax
An impact fee
A variance fee
questions.why: Impact fees are charged to developers to fund capacity their new project requires. Special assessments fall on existing owners whose parcels benefit.

questions.q: Under cumulative zoning, which of these is allowed?
options: A factory in a residential district
A house in a commercial district
Only the stated use in each district
Any use the city council approves
questions.why: Cumulative, or pyramid, zoning lets a higher use go into a lower district, but not the reverse. Allowing only the stated use is exclusive zoning.

questions.q: The store at 1402 Loblolly Boulevard opened legally before a 2010 rezoning to single-family. What is its status?
options: A nonconforming use that may continue
An illegal use that must close
A special exception needing board approval
A variance that ends when the store is sold
questions.why: A use that was legal when it began and no longer complies is grandfathered as nonconforming. A use that never complied is a violation.

ch19-variance-special-exception-rezoning.title: Variance, special exception, rezoning, spot zoning

questions.q: A homeowner wants to run a day care in a residential district whose ordinance allows it if conditions are met and the board approves. What does she need?
options: A variance
Spot zoning
A rezoning
A special exception
questions.why: A special exception permits a use the ordinance already anticipates, once conditions are met. A variance relaxes a dimensional rule like a setback.

questions.q: A listing licensee knows a Spoonbill Point Drive garage conversion was never permitted. What must she do?
options: Nothing, since checking permits is the buyer's job
Disclose it, since it materially affects value
Disclose it only if the buyer asks
Refuse the listing until the room is removed
questions.why: Florida requires sellers and licensees to disclose known facts that materially affect value and aren't readily observable. Unpermitted work isn't the buyer's risk alone.

questions.q: Who writes the building code a Florida county enforces?
options: Each county commission
The local building official
The state, through the Florida Building Code
FEMA
questions.why: Florida has one statewide code, maintained by the Florida Building Commission. Counties enforce it and may amend it only in limited ways.

questions.q: Zoning allows two-story homes, but the deed restrictions allow only one story. What may the owner build?
options: One story, because the stricter rule controls
Two stories, because zoning overrides private rules
Two stories, if the city issues a permit
Whatever the HOA votes to allow that year
questions.why: When private restrictions and zoning conflict, the more restrictive governs. Zoning doesn't override deed restrictions.

questions.q: A home sits in Zone X. Which statement is accurate?
options: The home has no flood risk
Flood insurance is mandatory for any loan
Flood insurance isn't mandatory, but flood risk still exists
A standard homeowner's policy covers flood there
questions.why: Zone X means moderate to minimal mapped risk, not none, and many flood claims come from outside the SFHA. Standard homeowner's policies don't cover flood anywhere.

questions.q: Who issues the extra permit needed to rebuild seaward of the coastal construction control line?
options: FEMA
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
Only the county building department
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection
questions.why: The CCCL is a Florida line, and building seaward of it needs a Florida DEP permit on top of local permits.

questions.q: Which transaction requires Florida's radon notice?
options: Only sales of single-family homes
The sale or rental of any building, residential or commercial
Only buildings with foundation cracks
Only buildings that failed a radon test
questions.why: The notice applies to the sale or rental of any building. The law requires the notice, not a test.

questions.q: The seller of a 1962 house on Loblolly Boulevard never tested for lead and knows of none. What is required?
options: The pamphlet, warning statement and disclosure stating no known lead
Nothing, since no lead is known

questions.q: Before buying the former dry cleaner at 2300 Loblolly Boulevard, how can an investor protect against cleanup liability?
options: Rely on the rule that only the polluter pays
Conduct a Phase I environmental site assessment
Order a radon test
Take title through an LLC
questions.why: CERCLA can make the current owner liable regardless of who caused the contamination. A Phase I before purchase supports the innocent landowner defense.

questions.q: A Florida home has sinkhole damage but stays habitable. When is the damage covered?
options: Always, since all sinkhole damage must be covered
Only if the home has a homestead exemption
Never, since sinkholes can't be insured in Florida
When the owner bought optional sinkhole coverage
questions.why: Florida requires coverage only for catastrophic ground cover collapse, which makes the home uninhabitable. Lesser damage generally needs optional coverage.
